coverage.title: Where your notes and the official objectives differ
coverage.intro: Your course tags some lessons with the wrong objective number. This quiz uses CompTIA's official V15 numbering:
coverage.watchTitle: Three things in the notes to watch for in the exam:
watch: The notes say data going into the cloud costs more. In practice providers usually charge for data going out (egress).

The notes list five steps. The official process has seven: investigate and verify, quarantine, disable System Restore, remediate, schedule scans and updates, enable System Restore and create a restore point, educate the end user.
The exam (US system) says Class C for electrical fires. In the UK, Class C means flammable gases and you'd use CO2 on electrical fires.

questions.q: How many pins does a DDR4 SO-DIMM module have?
questions.e: DDR4 SO-DIMMs have 260 pins. DDR3 SO-DIMMs have 204 and DDR5 SO-DIMMs have 262. 288 is the pin count for full-size DDR4/DDR5 desktop DIMMs, not laptop modules.

questions.q: A technician is ordering RAM for a laptop that takes DDR5 SO-DIMMs. Which pin count should the module have?
questions.e: DDR5 SO-DIMM is 262 pins. It's easy to mix up with DDR4 SO-DIMM (260), which is why the notes list all three: DDR3 204, DDR4 260, DDR5 262.

questions.q: What type of RAM do most smartphones and tablets use?
questions.e: Mobile devices commonly use RAM soldered to the board, so it can't be upgraded. Laptops are the devices that more often use removable SO-DIMMs.

questions.q: What are the dimensions of an M.2 2280 drive?
questions.e: The M.2 naming convention is width then length in millimetres. 2280 = 22mm wide by 80mm long, which is the most common size. 2230, 2242, 2260 and 22110 follow the same pattern.

questions.q: Which storage interface uses PCIe lanes and is significantly faster than SATA?
questions.e: NVMe (Non-Volatile Memory Express) runs over PCIe lanes and is much faster than SATA. mSATA is just a smaller SATA form factor, so it's still limited to SATA speeds (up to 6 Gbps).

questions.q: What is the maximum speed of the SATA interface?
questions.e: SATA goes up to 6 Gbps (SATA revisions run 1.5, 3 and 6 Gbps). If a drive needs more than that, you're looking at NVMe over PCIe.

questions.q: A customer wants a storage upgrade for a thin ultrabook that only has an mSATA slot. What should you tell them about performance?
o: mSATA is a smaller SATA variant, so it's still limited to SATA speeds
mSATA uses PCIe lanes, so it will match NVMe speeds
mSATA is a mechanical interface, so it will be slower than an HDD
mSATA only supports HDDs, not SSDs
questions.e: mSATA (Mini-SATA) is a space-saving form factor for compact devices but it's still SATA underneath, so the 6 Gbps ceiling applies. It does take SSDs.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an advantage of an SSD over an HDD?
questions.e: The notes list faster performance, greater durability (no moving parts) and lower power draw as SSD benefits. HDDs are still the cheaper option per gigabyte, which is why they're used for bulk storage.

questions.q: After replacing a laptop screen, the user complains Wi-Fi is now patchy. What is the most likely cause?
o: The Wi-Fi antenna wires were pinched or not re-routed along their original path
The SSD needs to be reformatted
questions.e: Laptop Wi-Fi antennas are routed through the display bezel and connect to the wireless card with delicate wires. If they get pinched, twisted or rerouted during reassembly, signal suffers. Always follow the original routing path.

questions.q: How do most laptops connect their internal wireless card?
questions.e: Laptops commonly use mini PCIe or M.2 slots for wireless cards. Phones and tablets use integrated wireless components instead.

questions.q: A smartphone has very poor battery life. You replace the battery. What kind of battery should you use and why?
o: An OEM battery, for best compatibility and performance
Any Li-ion battery with the same voltage, since they are interchangeable
A Ni-Cd battery, as it lasts longer
A generic battery, as long as the charger is also generic
questions.e: The notes' scenario has the tech fitting an OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) battery for compatibility and performance. Mobile batteries are usually Li-ion or LiPo, and vendor-specific chargers are advised because they're often proprietary.

questions.q: Which of these is a biometric security component found on mobile devices?
questions.e: Biometrics scan and recognise physical traits of the user: fingerprint scanners, facial recognition and voice recognition. NFC is a short-range communication feature, not biometric.

questions.q: What is the approximate range of Bluetooth on a typical mobile device?
questions.e: Bluetooth operates in the 2.4 GHz band with a typical range of around 10 m. 'A few centimetres' describes NFC.

questions.q: Which frequency band does Bluetooth use?
questions.e: Bluetooth uses the 2.4 GHz band, the same band as 802.11b/g/n Wi-Fi, which is why the two can interfere with each other.

questions.q: Which connector is Apple's proprietary standard for charging and data on iPhones and older iPads?
questions.e: Lightning is Apple's proprietary connector. Newer iPads (and recent iPhones) have moved to USB-C, but Lightning is the one to remember as Apple-proprietary.

questions.q: A traveller wants their laptop to use their phone's mobile data. Which feature should you set up?
questions.e: Tethering (or a mobile hotspot) shares the phone's internet connection. It can be done over Wi-Fi, USB or Bluetooth.

questions.q: Which three connection types can be used to tether a laptop to a smartphone?
questions.e: The notes list Wi-Fi (802.11), USB (wired) and Bluetooth (2.4 GHz) as tethering options. NFC's range and speed are far too limited to share an internet connection.

questions.q: A user needs to move large video files from a phone to a laptop quickly and charge the phone at the same time. What is the best option?
questions.e: USB-C supports high data rates and power delivery in one cable. Bluetooth and NFC are far slower and don't charge the phone.

questions.q: Which stylus features help a graphic designer draw naturally on a tablet?
questions.e: Styluses can support pressure sensitivity (lighter or heavier strokes), palm rejection (ignores your hand resting on the screen) and gestures.

questions.q: Which wired audio connector is commonly used by headsets and external speakers?
questions.e: The 3.5 mm TRS (tip-ring-sleeve) jack is the standard analogue audio connector. Headsets and speakers can also connect by USB, Bluetooth or Wi-Fi.

questions.q: Which file extension is used for Android app packages?
questions.e: .apk (Android Package Kit) is Android. .ipa is iOS/iPadOS, .dmg is macOS and .msi is a Windows installer.

questions.q: A developer gives you an app to install on a test iPad. What file extension would you expect?
questions.e: Both iOS and iPadOS use .ipa (iOS App Store Package) files.

questions.q: Which mobile OS is open source and used by many different manufacturers?
questions.e: Android is open source and gives OEMs lots of configuration options, which is why it appears on devices from many vendors. iOS and iPadOS only run on Apple hardware.

questions.q: A vendor has stopped releasing all updates and support for an OS version. What is this called?
questions.e: End-of-life is when the vendor stops updates and support altogether, which increases security risk. An update limitation is different: the OS is still supported but your older hardware can't run the new version.

questions.q: A client's old iPhone can't install the latest iOS version, even though Apple still updates iOS. What is this an example of?
questions.e: The OS is still supported, but the hardware is too old to take the new version. That's an update limitation: no new features or security fixes for that device.

questions.q: How does Android typically present its version numbers?
o: Version number plus a codename, e.g. Android 15 Vanilla Ice Cream
Build letters only, e.g. Android VIC
questions.e: Android uses a version number with a dessert-style codename (Android 15 Vanilla Ice Cream, Android 16 Baklava). iOS and iPadOS use major.minor.patch, e.g. 16.4.2.

questions.q: A phone has been dropped in a sink and won't turn on. What should you do first?
o: Don't plug it in or power it on; let it ventilate and dry out
Plug it into a charger to see if it responds
Hold the power button to force a restart
Put it in a warm oven to speed up drying
questions.e: With liquid damage, don't connect power or power cycle it, as that can short the circuitry. Give it ventilation and plenty of time to dry, and look for visible signs of moisture.

questions.q: You notice a phone's back cover is bulging and the frame looks expanded. What is the most likely cause?
questions.e: Internal chemical reactions can make a battery swell, which pushes the case apart. It's a safety risk: handle with care and follow the manufacturer's replacement guidance.

questions.q: A device only charges when the cable is held at a certain angle. What should you check first?
o: The charging port and cable for damage
questions.e: That's classic improper charging. Inspect the charging port, the cable and adapter for damage, and confirm the power outlet works.

questions.q: A user says none of their wireless connections work: no Wi-Fi, no Bluetooth, no mobile data. What is the quickest thing to check?
o: Whether Airplane Mode is turned on
questions.e: Airplane Mode disables all the wireless radios at once. It's the first thing to rule out when everything wireless is down together.

questions.q: A tablet's touch input is consistently a few millimetres off from where the user taps. What is this called and what should you try?
o: Cursor drift; clean the screen and run touchscreen recalibration
Broken screen; replace the display immediately
questions.e: Misaligned touch input is cursor drift / a touch calibration issue. Clean the screen with a lint-free cloth and use the recalibration settings if the device has them.

questions.q: A tablet gets very hot while gaming in the garden on a sunny day. Which steps are appropriate?
o: Move it out of direct sunlight and close unused apps
Put it in the fridge to cool down quickly
questions.e: Overheating comes from heavy use, environment and too many open apps. Check resource usage, get it out of direct sunlight and close what isn't needed.

questions.q: A tablet doesn't recognise its active stylus. Which check is specific to active styluses?
questions.e: Active styluses have electronics inside and need power. The notes also say to verify compatibility and inspect for physical damage.

questions.q: A two-year-old phone opens apps much more slowly than when new. Which is NOT one of the recommended steps?
o: Make sure there is enough free storage
questions.e: For degraded performance, the notes say verify OS updates, check storage, close unused apps and uninstall unneeded ones. The digitizer is the touch layer and has nothing to do with app speed.

questions.q: A user's app keeps freezing and crashing. What is the best first step?
questions.e: Force quitting clears an immediate crash or conflict. Updating the app, freeing memory and rebooting come next. A full OS reinstall is a last resort.
questions.l: Troubleshooting mobile OS and app issues

questions.q: An OS update keeps failing and the phone shows a low storage warning. What is the most likely cause?
questions.e: OS updates need a good amount of free space. If the hardware were unsupported, the update usually wouldn't be offered at all.
questions.l: Troubleshooting mobile OS and app issues

questions.q: A phone's screen won't rotate when turned sideways. Which is NOT a likely cause?
o: Rotation lock is enabled in settings
questions.e: Autorotate problems come from rotation settings, a faulty gyroscope or motion sensor, or a frozen OS. Fix by enabling rotation, running a sensor diagnostic or restarting. Wi-Fi has nothing to do with it.
questions.l: Troubleshooting mobile OS and app issues

questions.q: A phone restarts randomly several times a day, starting shortly after the user installed some new apps. What should you try first?
questions.e: Random reboots can come from hardware faults, corrupted OS files or rogue apps. The timing points at the new apps, so uninstalling them is the sensible first step before diagnostics or an OS reinstall.
questions.l: Troubleshooting mobile OS and app issues

questions.q: A user's Bluetooth earbuds keep disconnecting from their phone. Which fix is listed for Bluetooth problems?
o: Reboot both devices and re-pair them, and update firmware
questions.e: For Bluetooth: reset the Bluetooth device, update firmware and re-pair after rebooting both. Causes include interference, outdated firmware and incompatibility.
questions.l: Troubleshooting mobile OS and app issues

questions.q: Contactless payment works on and off for a user. Which is a common cause of NFC problems?
o: The devices aren't aligned properly during the tap
The screen resolution is too high
questions.e: NFC only works over a few centimetres, so misalignment is common. Also check NFC is enabled in settings, look for interference and restart the device.
questions.l: Troubleshooting mobile OS and app issues

questions.q: An app won't install on a user's phone. Which set of causes fits this symptom?
o: OS incompatibility, lack of storage, wrong account login
Gyroscope fault, frozen OS, rotation lock
Swollen battery, damaged port, liquid damage
questions.e: Failed installs come from the app not supporting the OS version, not enough storage or being signed in with the wrong account. Fix those and restart the installation.
questions.l: Troubleshooting mobile OS and app issues

questions.q: A smartphone shows lots of pop-up ads even when no apps are open. What is the most likely cause?
questions.e: Adware injects ads into apps and browsers. Remove the infected apps, clear browser cache/app data and use antivirus or ad-blocking software.

questions.q: What is the main security risk of rooting an Android phone or jailbreaking an iPhone?
o: It bypasses built-in security restrictions, increasing exposure to malware
It downgrades the OS to an EOL version
questions.e: Rooting/jailbreaking gives the user full system privileges by bypassing the vendor's security model. That leaves the device far more exposed to malware and unauthorised access. MDM can be used to enforce policies against it.

questions.q: A user downloads what looks like their bank's app, but it turns out to be a fake made to steal logins. What is this called?
questions.e: Spoofed apps mimic legitimate ones to trick users, exploiting trust in familiar brands. Check the publisher before installing and only use trusted stores.

questions.q: Why should developer mode be turned off on a mobile device when it isn't needed?
o: It exposes debugging features and can allow unauthorised app installs
It drains the battery by keeping the screen on
questions.e: Developer mode exposes debugging and system-level features and can bypass some security restrictions, including allowing installs from outside the official store.

questions.q: A user gets a text from their carrier warning they've almost used their monthly data, but they've barely used the phone. What should you do?
o: Run a malware scan and check data usage per app
questions.e: Unexpected data use points to malware or a misconfigured app. Scan for malware, check per-app data usage, remove or update the culprit and use Wi-Fi where possible.

questions.q: A phone keeps showing urgent 'Your device is infected! Tap here to clean' alerts from an app the user doesn't recognise. What is the right advice?
o: Don't tap the alerts; remove the rogue app and use trusted security software
Tap the alert and follow its instructions
Ignore it, as these are normal OS notifications
Root the device to remove the alerts
questions.e: Fake security warnings come from rogue apps pretending to be security software. Don't interact with them, remove the app causing them and use a trusted security app.

questions.q: A user's contacts say they're receiving odd messages from the user's messaging app that the user never sent. Which symptom is this?
questions.e: Apps doing things on their own, like sending messages, is unexpected application behaviour, usually from malware modifying the app. Update/reinstall the app, scan for malware and reboot.

questions.q: An app from an unofficial store is using a huge amount of network bandwidth. What is the best fix?
o: Remove the app and use a network monitoring tool to watch traffic
Update every app from that unofficial store
questions.e: High network traffic from an untrusted app suggests spyware sending data out. Remove it, and monitor traffic to confirm the problem has gone.

questions.q: On an iPhone, where would you go to turn mobile data on or off and monitor how much each app has used?
questions.e: In iOS, Settings > Cellular (Mobile Data in UK builds) lets you enable/disable cellular data, see plan options and monitor usage.

questions.q: On a typical Android phone, where would you enable NFC and set up contactless payments?
o: Settings > Connections > NFC and contactless payment
questions.e: The notes' Android demo shows Settings > Connections, which holds Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and NFC and contactless payment. Exact menu names vary by manufacturer.

questions.q: Which device connects endpoints within a LAN and forwards traffic using MAC addresses?
questions.e: Switches work inside the LAN and make forwarding decisions on MAC addresses. Routers move traffic between different networks using IP addresses.

questions.q: A small team wants to share files directly between their laptops without buying a server. Which network model is this?
questions.e: In peer-to-peer, each device acts as both client and server and shares resources directly. It avoids the cost of a server but doesn't scale or secure well.

questions.q: Which fibre type is best for linking two data centres in different cities?
questions.e: Single-mode is for long distances (WANs). Multi-mode is for shorter runs, such as linking switches across a campus.

questions.q: Which type of copper cabling is typically used for cable internet connections?
questions.e: Coaxial cable is used for cable internet (and cable TV). Twisted pair (Cat5e, Cat6) is used for Ethernet.

questions.q: In a network, what does a client do?
o: Requests services or data from servers
Forwards frames based on MAC addresses
questions.e: Clients request, servers provide, and peers do both. Switches and routers are redistribution points, not endpoints.

questions.q: Which port does SSH use?
questions.e: SSH is port 22 and gives encrypted command-line access. Telnet (23) does the same job unencrypted, which is why it's been replaced by SSH.

questions.q: Which port is used by RDP?
questions.e: Remote Desktop Protocol uses port 3389 for graphical remote access to Windows machines.

questions.q: Which port does SMB/CIFS use for Windows file and printer sharing?
questions.e: SMB/CIFS uses 445. Don't mix it up with 137 to 139 (the older NetBIOS/NetBT services) or 389 (LDAP).

questions.q: Which port is used by LDAP?
questions.e: LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) uses port 389 to talk to directory services such as user authentication. Don't confuse it with RDP on 3389.

questions.q: What are FTP ports 20 and 21 each used for?
o: 20 for data transfer, 21 for control commands
20 for control commands, 21 for data transfer
questions.e: FTP uses port 21 for control (commands) and port 20 for the actual data transfer.

questions.q: A user checks email on a phone, a laptop and a tablet and wants all three to stay in sync. Which protocol and port should the client use?
questions.e: IMAP keeps mail on the server and syncs across devices. POP3 downloads mail for local, offline access, so it doesn't sync well across multiple devices. SMTP is for sending.

questions.q: Which protocol and port are used to send email between mail servers?
questions.e: SMTP (port 25) sends mail to and between servers. POP3 and IMAP are for retrieving mail.

questions.q: Which ports does DHCP use?
questions.e: DHCP uses 67 (server) and 68 (client). Port 53 is DNS.

questions.q: Which port does DNS use?
questions.e: DNS uses port 53 to resolve names into IP addresses.

questions.q: An old system on the network still uses ports 137 to 139. What protocol is this?
questions.e: NetBIOS over TCP/IP uses 137 (name service), 138 (datagram service) and 139 (session service). It's legacy Windows networking; the notes' scenario isolates such systems for security.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes TCP compared with UDP?
o: TCP is connection-oriented and reliable; UDP is connectionless and faster with no delivery guarantee
TCP is connectionless; UDP is connection-oriented
Both guarantee delivery, but UDP encrypts traffic
UDP is used for email; TCP is used for video streaming
questions.e: TCP sets up a connection and uses error checking and retransmission, so it's used for email and web. UDP skips all that, making it better for real-time traffic like video calls and gaming.

questions.q: A video conferencing app needs the lowest possible latency and can cope with the odd lost packet. Which transport protocol suits it?
questions.e: UDP is connectionless, with no retransmission delay, which suits real-time voice and video.

questions.q: Which organisation manages the global allocation of IP addresses and port numbers?
questions.e: The Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) coordinates IP addresses and port numbers so they're unique and standardised.

questions.q: Which three channels are the non-overlapping channels in the 2.4 GHz band?
questions.e: 2.4 GHz only has three non-overlapping channels (1, 6, 11), which is why it gets congested. 36, 40 and 44 are 5 GHz channels.

questions.q: Which Wi-Fi band has the shortest range but the most channels and lowest latency?
questions.e: 6 GHz (Wi-Fi 6E) gives high speed, low latency and lots of channels, but the shortest range. 2.4 GHz is the opposite: best range, slowest, most interference.

questions.q: Which 802.11 standard introduced MIMO and works on both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz?
questions.e: 802.11n (up to 600 Mbps) was dual-band and introduced MIMO. 802.11ac then added MU-MIMO on 5 GHz.

questions.q: Which 802.11 standard introduced MU-MIMO and runs only on the 5 GHz band?
questions.e: 802.11ac is 5 GHz only and introduced MU-MIMO for better multi-user performance.

questions.q: Which standard is known as Wi-Fi 6/6E and can use 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz?
questions.e: 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6, or 6E when using 6 GHz) supports up to 9.6 Gbps and is designed for high-density environments.

questions.q: Which two standards are limited to 54 Mbps?
questions.e: 802.11a (5 GHz) and 802.11g (2.4 GHz) both top out at 54 Mbps. 802.11b is 11 Mbps on 2.4 GHz, and g is backward compatible with b.

questions.q: A university lecture hall has hundreds of devices connecting at once. Which standard is optimised for this kind of high-density environment?
questions.e: Wi-Fi 6 is designed for efficiency with many simultaneous connections.

questions.q: In a block of flats with lots of neighbouring Wi-Fi networks, which band should you prioritise to reduce interference while keeping wide device support?
questions.e: 5 GHz has many more non-overlapping channels than 2.4 GHz and less interference. 6 GHz is even cleaner but older devices may not support it.

questions.q: What frequency does NFC operate at?
questions.e: NFC runs at 13.56 MHz over a range of a few centimetres. RFID can use low, high or ultra-high frequencies depending on the application.

questions.q: A warehouse wants to track pallets automatically as they pass through doorways. Which technology fits best?
questions.e: RFID uses tags to identify and track objects. Ultra-high frequency RFID tags can be read at longer distances, which suits warehouse tracking.

questions.q: Which server collects log data from switches, firewalls and other devices in one place?
questions.e: Syslog collects, stores and forwards log data from network devices for monitoring and troubleshooting.

questions.q: Why is an NTP server important for troubleshooting?
o: It keeps device clocks in sync so log timestamps line up
It assigns IP addresses to clients
It filters spam before it reaches inboxes
It balances traffic across web servers
questions.e: Network Time Protocol synchronises clocks. Without it, log entries from different devices won't match up, making troubleshooting and security investigations much harder.

questions.q: A single appliance at the network edge provides firewall, intrusion detection and anti-virus. What is it?
questions.e: A UTM combines several security functions into one device.

questions.q: An online shop's website slows down at peak times. Which device spreads incoming traffic across several web servers?
questions.e: Load balancers distribute traffic across multiple servers to improve performance and reliability.

questions.q: A company wants to cache frequently visited websites and filter what staff can browse. Which device does this?
questions.e: A proxy server sits between clients and external networks, providing caching, access control/filtering and anonymity.

questions.q: What does AAA stand for in network services?
questions.e: AAA servers manage who you are (authentication), what you can do (authorisation) and logging what you did (accounting).

questions.q: A water treatment plant uses a control system to monitor industrial processes. What is this system called, and how should it be protected?
o: SCADA; isolate it from the corporate network with strict access controls
IoT; connect it to guest Wi-Fi for easy access
UTM; expose it to the internet for remote monitoring
NTP; synchronise it with public time servers only
questions.e: SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) runs industrial processes. These legacy/embedded systems are critical, so the notes' scenario isolates them from the corporate network.

questions.q: Which DNS record maps a domain name to an IPv6 address?
questions.e: A records are IPv4, AAAA records are IPv6. An easy way to remember: IPv6 addresses are four times longer, so four As.

questions.q: Which DNS record tells other servers where to deliver email for a domain?
questions.e: The Mail Exchanger (MX) record points to the domain's mail server.

questions.q: You want support.company.com to point to the same host as helpdesk.company.com. Which record do you create?
questions.e: A CNAME (canonical name) maps an alias to another host record, simplifying DNS management.

questions.q: Which email security record lists the mail servers allowed to send email on behalf of a domain?
questions.e: SPF (Sender Policy Framework) lists authorised senders. DKIM adds a cryptographic signature to the headers, and DMARC builds on both with policies and reporting.

questions.q: An admin wants receiving servers to reject mail that fails SPF and DKIM checks, and to get reports about the failures. What should they configure?
questions.e: DMARC builds on SPF and DKIM, adding policy (what to do with failures) and reporting.

questions.q: Which email authentication method adds a digital signature to email headers so receivers can verify the domain and that the message wasn't altered?
questions.e: DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) signs outgoing mail. SPF only checks which servers are allowed to send.

questions.q: A technician needs to stop the DHCP server handing out 192.168.1.1 to 192.168.1.10, which are used by servers with static IPs. What should they configure?
questions.e: Exclusions remove addresses from the scope so DHCP never assigns them. A reservation is different: it always gives one particular device (by MAC address) the same address.

questions.q: A network printer must always get the same IP address from DHCP. What should you set up?
o: A DHCP reservation based on the printer's MAC address
questions.e: Reservations tie a specific IP to a specific MAC address, so the printer gets the same address every time.

questions.q: In DHCP, what is a scope?
o: The range of IP addresses available for assignment
How long a device can keep its address
An address tied to one MAC address
A list of blocked MAC addresses
questions.e: The scope is the address pool. The lease is how long a device keeps an address, and a reservation ties an address to one device.

questions.q: What is a TXT record commonly used for?
o: Domain verification and security information, such as SPF
Mapping a name to an IPv4 address
Directing email to the mail server
Creating an alias for another host
questions.e: TXT records hold human- or machine-readable text, often for domain verification (e.g. Google Workspace) and email security like SPF.

questions.q: A company needs to permanently connect its London and Manchester office networks securely over the internet. Which type of VPN fits?
questions.e: Site-to-site VPNs connect whole networks at different locations. Remote access VPNs connect a single user to a private network.

questions.q: An employee working from a café needs secure access to company servers. What should IT provide?
questions.e: A remote access VPN creates an encrypted tunnel over the untrusted public Wi-Fi to the corporate network.

questions.q: Which is a benefit of VLANs?
o: Reduced broadcast traffic and better security through segmentation
questions.e: VLANs logically segment a physical network. That limits access between groups, cuts broadcast traffic and simplifies management. They don't encrypt anything; that's a VPN's job.

questions.q: How does a switch know which VLAN an Ethernet frame belongs to when it travels between switches?
o: A VLAN tag is added to the frame
The frame is encrypted with the VLAN key
The DHCP lease includes the VLAN
questions.e: VLAN tagging adds a tag to Ethernet frames identifying the VLAN, so switches can forward traffic correctly.

questions.q: Which OSI layer are routers associated with?
questions.e: Routers forward packets using IP addresses, a Layer 3 function. Switches are traditionally Layer 2 (MAC addresses), though some can also route.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a managed and an unmanaged switch?
o: Managed switches support features like VLANs, QoS and SNMP; unmanaged switches are plug-and-play with no configuration
Managed switches are wireless; unmanaged switches are wired
Managed switches can only be used in homes
questions.e: Managed switches offer configuration and monitoring. Unmanaged switches simply connect devices and suit small, simple networks.

questions.q: How much power does standard PoE (IEEE 802.3af) provide per port?
questions.e: 802.3af (PoE) provides up to 15.4 W. 802.3at (PoE+) provides more, with the notes giving 25.5 W for devices like PTZ cameras.

questions.q: You need to power one IP camera in a spot with no power socket, and the existing switch doesn't support PoE. What is the simplest fix?
questions.e: A PoE injector adds power to a single Ethernet run. For lots of devices, a PoE switch is tidier.

questions.q: What does an ONT do in a fibre-to-the-home installation?
o: Converts fibre optic signals into electrical signals for the router
Converts DSL signals for phone lines
questions.e: An Optical Network Terminal converts light signals from the ISP's fibre into electrical/Ethernet signals.

questions.q: Which standard lets cable modems deliver internet over coaxial cable TV networks?
questions.e: DOCSIS (Data Over Cable Service Interface Specification) carries data over existing cable TV infrastructure.

questions.q: Which statement about a MAC address is correct?
o: It is a unique hardware identifier assigned to a NIC, shown in hexadecimal
It is assigned by DHCP each time a device connects
It identifies the network portion of an IP address
questions.e: A MAC address is a hardware-based ID on each NIC, written like 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E. The first half identifies the manufacturer.

questions.q: What is a lightweight access point?
o: A simple AP managed centrally by a Wireless LAN Controller (WLC)
An AP that works without any wired connection
An AP that also acts as a cable modem
questions.e: Lightweight APs are controlled centrally through a WLC. Standalone APs manage their own wireless communications.

questions.q: What is a patch panel used for?
o: Terminating and organising network cable runs in one central place
questions.e: A patch panel is where structured cabling terminates, making connections easy to manage and troubleshoot.

questions.q: A PC shows an IP address of 169.254.12.7 and can't reach the internet. What does this tell you?
o: It couldn't get an address from DHCP and has fallen back to APIPA
It has a valid public IP address
It has been given a static IP
questions.e: 169.254.x.y is APIPA, used when DHCP isn't available. It allows local communication only, with no internet access. Check the DHCP server and the connection.

questions.q: Which of these is a private IPv4 address?
questions.e: Private ranges are 10.0.0.0 to 10.255.255.255, 172.16.0.0 to 172.31.255.255 and 192.168.0.0 to 192.168.255.255. 172.32.x.x is just outside the Class B private range, and 192.169 is not 192.168.

questions.q: What is the default subnet mask for a Class B address?
questions.e: Class A is /8, Class B is /16 and Class C is /24. Classes D (multicast) and E (experimental) have no default mask.

questions.q: Which address range is Class D, used for multicast?
questions.e: Class D (224 to 239) is multicast. 192 to 223 is Class C, 128 to 191 is Class B and 240 upwards is Class E.

questions.q: How long is an IPv6 address?
questions.e: IPv6 is 128 bits written in colon-separated hexadecimal. IPv4 is 32 bits in dotted decimal. 48 bits is the length of a MAC address.

questions.q: Which is a correct shortened form of 2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334?
questions.e: Leading zeros in each block can be dropped, and one run of all-zero blocks can be replaced by ::. You can only use :: once, and you can't just delete blocks without it.

questions.q: What does a subnet mask do?
o: Separates the network portion of an IP address from the host portion
questions.e: The mask's contiguous 1 bits mark the network part and the 0 bits mark the host part. 255.255.255.0 means the first three octets are the network.

questions.q: A PC can talk to other PCs on its subnet but can't reach anything on the internet. Its IP and mask are correct. Which setting is most likely wrong?
questions.e: Traffic for other networks goes to the default gateway (usually the router). If that's missing or wrong, local traffic works but nothing leaves the subnet.

questions.q: Which is a drawback of static IP addressing?
o: It doesn't scale well and is prone to human error
It changes every time the device reboots
questions.e: Static addresses are good for servers and printers that must stay fixed, but they're manual, so they don't scale and are easy to misconfigure. Dynamic (DHCP) addressing fixes both.

questions.q: A remote cottage has no phone line or cable but has a clear view of the southern sky. Which internet type is most suitable?
questions.e: Satellite reaches remote locations without wired infrastructure. Downsides: high latency and weather-dependent performance.

questions.q: Which internet connection type is known for high latency and being affected by weather?
questions.e: Satellite signals travel a huge distance to space and back, giving high latency, and heavy weather can degrade them.

questions.q: Which connection type shares bandwidth with other users in the neighbourhood?
questions.e: Cable broadband is shared within a neighbourhood, so speeds can drop at busy times. DSL gives a dedicated connection per user but is sensitive to distance from the exchange.

questions.q: Which variant of DSL has different upload and download speeds and is common in homes?
questions.e: ADSL is asymmetric: faster download than upload. VDSL is the very-high-speed variant.

questions.q: A rural home gets internet from a provider using a roof-mounted receiver that needs line of sight to a nearby mast. What type of connection is this?
questions.e: A Wireless Internet Service Provider delivers internet by radio, typically to rural areas, and needs line of sight.

questions.q: Which network type provides servers with high-speed, block-level access to storage, often using Fibre Channel or iSCSI?
questions.e: A Storage Area Network is dedicated to storage and gives block-level access.

questions.q: A city council links its libraries and offices across the city using high-speed fibre. What type of network is this?
questions.e: A Metropolitan Area Network connects multiple LANs across a city-sized area.

questions.q: Your phone, smartwatch and wireless earbuds connected via Bluetooth form which type of network?
questions.e: A Personal Area Network covers personal devices within a short range, usually about 10 m with Bluetooth.

questions.q: Which tool attaches RJ-45 connectors to the end of an Ethernet cable?
questions.e: A crimper presses the connector pins into the wires. A punchdown tool is for terminating wires onto patch panels and keystone jacks.

questions.q: Which tool is used to terminate individual wires onto a patch panel or keystone jack?
questions.e: The punchdown tool pushes each wire into the IDC terminals on a punchdown block.

questions.q: A cable in the comms room isn't labelled and you need to find where the other end is. Which tool should you use?
questions.e: A toner probe is two parts: the toner puts a signal on the cable and the probe detects it at the other end.

questions.q: You want to check whether a server's NIC port works without connecting it to the network. Which tool should you use?
questions.e: A loopback plug sends the port's output signal straight back into its input, so you can test the port in isolation.

questions.q: A security analyst wants to capture traffic between a router and switch without disrupting it. Which device should they use?
questions.e: A network tap gives passive access to traffic for monitoring and analysis without interrupting the flow.

questions.q: Before deploying newly installed cables, a technician wants to confirm they're wired correctly with no split pairs. Which tool should they use?
questions.e: A cable tester verifies continuity and wiring. Advanced ones detect split pairs and crosstalk.

questions.q: What is the correct UNC path format to open a shared folder on a server in File Explorer?
questions.e: UNC (Universal Naming Convention) paths start with two backslashes followed by the server name, then the share name.

questions.q: A user connects to Wi-Fi in a coffee shop. Which Windows network profile should they choose and why?
o: Public, because it uses more restrictive settings for untrusted networks
Private, because it allows file and printer sharing
questions.e: Public is the restrictive profile for untrusted networks. Private relaxes sharing and discovery for trusted networks like home.

questions.q: A laptop uses a mobile hotspot with a small data allowance. How can you stop Windows using lots of data in the background for updates?
o: Set it as a private network
questions.e: A metered connection tells Windows to limit background data use, such as some updates.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a domain and a workgroup?
o: A domain uses a domain controller for central authentication and management; a workgroup is decentralised with each PC managed separately
A workgroup needs a server; a domain doesn't
Domains are only for home use
Workgroups support more computers than domains
questions.e: Domains centralise accounts and policy on a domain controller and suit businesses. Workgroups suit small or home networks where each PC manages its own accounts.

questions.q: A company wants all employee web traffic to pass through a content-filtering server. What should be configured on each Windows client?
questions.e: Proxy settings route traffic through a proxy server for filtering, caching, access control or anonymity.

questions.q: What does WWAN refer to in Windows network settings?
o: A cellular/mobile data connection, e.g. via a SIM card
questions.e: Wireless Wide Area Network means cellular internet (3G, 4G LTE, 5G), such as a laptop with a built-in SIM slot.

questions.q: Which Windows command shows a PC's IP address, subnet mask and default gateway?
questions.e: ipconfig displays interface configuration. Add /all for more detail (DNS servers, MAC address, DHCP info) or /release and /renew to refresh a DHCP lease.

questions.q: Which Windows command combines ping and tracert to show packet loss and latency at each hop?
questions.e: pathping traces the route and then gathers loss and latency stats for every hop. It's slower than tracert but more detailed.

questions.q: Which command maps a shared folder to drive Z: on Windows?
questions.e: net use maps or disconnects network drives. net use * /delete removes all mappings. net user manages user accounts, which is a common mix-up.

questions.q: Which command shows active network connections and listening ports on a Windows PC?
questions.e: netstat lists active connections, listening ports and routing tables. netstat -a shows all connections and listening ports.

questions.q: Which Windows command shows the current logged-in user, and with /groups lists their group memberships?
questions.e: whoami shows the current user and domain; whoami /groups lists groups. hostname shows the computer name.

questions.q: On a Linux machine, which command queries DNS for information about a domain?
questions.e: dig queries DNS servers (dig +short shows just the IP). On Windows the equivalent is nslookup.

questions.q: Which Linux command shows network interfaces and their IP addresses?
questions.e: The ip command shows and configures addresses and interfaces. ip link set eth0 up enables an interface.

questions.q: A developer wants to fetch only the HTTP headers from a web server on Linux. Which command should they use?
questions.e: curl transfers data with protocols like HTTP, HTTPS and FTP. The -I option fetches only the headers.

questions.q: How do you display the help and available options for a Windows command such as ping?
questions.e: Adding /? to most Windows commands shows their usage and options.

questions.q: VoIP calls in an office have choppy audio and delays. What should the technician implement to prioritise voice traffic?
questions.e: QoS prioritises real-time traffic like VoIP. The causes of poor VoIP quality are jitter, latency, packet loss and lack of bandwidth.

questions.q: What is jitter?
o: Variation in packet delay over time
A port going up and down repeatedly
questions.e: Jitter is inconsistent packet delay, which hurts real-time apps like VoIP and video calls. Use pathping to find congestion and QoS to prioritise real-time traffic.

questions.q: A switch port keeps going up and down every few seconds. Which is NOT a likely cause?
questions.e: Port flapping comes from bad cables/NICs, duplex mismatches and loops. DNS settings don't affect whether a physical link stays up.

questions.q: Users can access local file shares but not the internet. Which first step makes most sense?
o: Run ipconfig to check the gateway and DNS settings
questions.e: Limited connectivity usually means a wrong gateway/DNS, a DHCP problem or an ISP/modem failure. ipconfig shows the settings, and pinging the gateway and an external IP narrows it down.

questions.q: Wi-Fi drops every time someone uses the staff room microwave. What type of issue is this and what helps?
o: External interference; use a Wi-Fi analyser and move APs to non-overlapping channels or 5 GHz
questions.e: Microwaves, cordless phones and neighbouring networks all interfere with 2.4 GHz. A Wi-Fi analyser finds the source, and you can change channels or reposition devices.

questions.q: Several users can't log into network resources. Where on Windows can you review the failed login attempts?
questions.e: Event Viewer's Security log records failed logons. Then reset credentials or unlock accounts, and check authentication servers like RADIUS or Active Directory.

questions.q: Users in the UK complain an app hosted in Australia is slow to respond. Which tool helps show where along the path the delay happens?
questions.e: High latency needs path analysis. tracert (or pathping) shows each hop and the delay at that point.

questions.q: Which LCD panel type offers the best colour accuracy and widest viewing angles?
questions.e: In-plane switching gives superior colour accuracy and viewing angles, so it suits designers and photo editing. TN is fastest but has poor colour and angles; VA has the best contrast of the three LCD types.

questions.q: A competitive gamer wants the fastest response time to reduce motion blur, and colour accuracy doesn't matter. Which LCD panel type fits?
questions.e: Twisted nematic has the fastest response time of the LCD panel types, often paired with high refresh rates, at the cost of colour and viewing angles.

questions.q: Which LCD panel type gives the deepest blacks and best contrast ratio of the three LCD panel types?
questions.e: Vertical alignment panels have better contrast than IPS and TN, which is why they're popular in TVs.

questions.q: Why can OLED displays show true blacks?
o: Each pixel emits its own light and can switch off completely, so no backlight is needed
They use thousands of tiny LEDs with local dimming
They use a CCFL backlight with an inverter
They use a VA panel layer
questions.e: OLED pixels are self-emissive organic compounds, so a black pixel is simply off. Mini-LED is a backlight technology for LCDs that improves contrast with local dimming zones.

questions.q: An older laptop screen is very dim and flickers. The display uses a CCFL backlight. Which component is most likely failing?
questions.e: The inverter converts DC to AC for CCFL backlights. A failing inverter causes dim or flickering screens. Modern LED-backlit screens don't need one because LEDs run on DC.

questions.q: What does a digitizer do?
o: Converts touch input into digital signals
Converts DC power to AC for the backlight
questions.e: The digitizer is the touch layer. Capacitive touch screens (most common) detect touch electrically; resistive ones use pressure-sensitive layers.

questions.q: What does refresh rate measure?
o: How many times per second the display updates its image, in Hz
How many pixels are packed into each inch
The range of colours a display can produce
The time taken for a pixel to change colour
questions.e: Refresh rate is in hertz. 60 Hz is standard, 120 to 144 Hz is common for gaming, and 240 Hz+ is for esports. Pixel density is PPI and colour gamut is the colour range.

questions.q: Two 27-inch monitors are side by side: one is 1080p and one is 4K. Which statement is true?
o: The 4K monitor has a higher pixel density (PPI), so it looks sharper
Both have the same pixel density because the screens are the same size
The 1080p monitor has a higher pixel density
Pixel density depends only on refresh rate
questions.e: Pixel density is pixels per inch. More pixels on the same size of screen means a higher PPI and a sharper image.

questions.q: Which colour gamut is preferred for professional photography and print work?
questions.e: Adobe RGB is preferred for photography and printing. sRGB is the standard for web/office, and DCI-P3 is used for cinematic and HDR content. CMYK is a print colour model, not a display gamut.

questions.q: What is the resolution of 4K (UHD)?
questions.e: 4K is 3840 x 2160. 1920 x 1080 is Full HD and 2560 x 1440 is QHD.

questions.q: What is the maximum data rate of USB 2.0?
questions.e: USB 2.0 is 480 Mbps. USB 3.0 raised that to 5 Gbps.

questions.q: What is the maximum data rate of USB 3.0?
questions.e: USB 3.0 runs at up to 5 Gbps. 40 Gbps is Thunderbolt 3/4.

questions.q: Which connector do Thunderbolt 3 and 4 use?
questions.e: Thunderbolt 1 and 2 used Mini DisplayPort, and Thunderbolt 3 and 4 use USB-C with up to 40 Gbps and up to 100 W power delivery.

questions.q: Which video connector is analogue only and uses a 15-pin DE-15 connector?
questions.e: VGA is analogue and uses the 15-pin DE-15 connector. HDMI and DisplayPort are digital. DVI comes in DVI-D (digital), DVI-A (analogue) and DVI-I (both).

questions.q: Which DVI type carries both analogue and digital signals?
questions.e: DVI-I is Integrated (both). DVI-D is digital only and DVI-A is analogue only.

questions.q: A restaurant's old receipt printer connects to its till PC with a 9-pin RS-232 cable. What connector is this?
questions.e: DB9 is the 9-pin serial (RS-232) connector, still used for legacy POS equipment and network device console access.

questions.q: Which 4-pin connector was used to power older IDE hard drives and optical drives from the PSU?
questions.e: Molex is the 4-pin legacy peripheral power connector. Modern drives use the 15-pin SATA power connector.

questions.q: Which video cable carries digital audio and video and is the standard connection for TVs and games consoles?
questions.e: HDMI carries digital audio and video. It comes in Standard (Type A), Mini (Type C) and Micro (Type D) connectors.

questions.q: A laptop has only USB-C ports and the meeting room projector only has HDMI. What should you use?
questions.e: USB-C can carry video using DisplayPort Alt Mode, so a USB-C to HDMI adapter is the simple fix.

questions.q: What is the maximum speed of Cat5e?
questions.e: Cat5e supports 1 Gbps. Cat6 supports 10 Gbps up to 55 m, and Cat6a supports 10 Gbps up to 100 m.

questions.q: You need 10 Gbps over a 90-metre cable run. Which category should you install?
questions.e: Cat6 only does 10 Gbps up to 55 m. Cat6a extends 10 Gbps to the full 100 m.

questions.q: Network cable is being run through the air-handling space above a suspended office ceiling. Which cable is required?
questions.e: Plenum-rated cable has fire-retardant insulation that doesn't give off toxic smoke, which matters in spaces that circulate air.

questions.q: Which cable is designed to be buried underground between buildings without conduit?
questions.e: Direct burial cable has extra waterproof insulation to withstand moisture and soil.

questions.q: A factory floor has heavy machinery generating lots of electromagnetic interference. Which twisted-pair cable is best?
questions.e: STP adds shielding to reduce EMI, so it suits high-interference environments. UTP relies only on the twists.

questions.q: Which wiring standard is most common in modern Ethernet installations?
questions.e: Both come from TIA/EIA-568. T568B is the most common in modern commercial and residential cabling. T568A is older and used in some government/legacy installs.

questions.q: How many pins does an RJ-45 connector have?
questions.e: RJ-45 has 8 pins and is the Ethernet connector. RJ-11 (4 or 6 pins) is for phone lines and DSL.

questions.q: Which connector screws onto coaxial cable for cable TV and broadband?
questions.e: F-type is a screw-on coax connector. BNC is a twist-and-lock bayonet coax connector used for CCTV and old 10BASE2 networks.

questions.q: Which fibre connector is a small form-factor push-pull connector used in high-density installations?
questions.e: LC is the small form-factor fibre connector. SC is a larger push-pull fibre connector.

questions.q: Compared with multimode fibre, single-mode fibre has:
o: A smaller core and much longer reach
A larger core and shorter reach
questions.e: Single-mode has a tiny 8 to 10 micron core and reaches up to about 100 km. Multimode has a 50 to 62.5 micron core and reaches around 550 m.

questions.q: Which HDD spindle speed is typical of a standard consumer laptop drive?
questions.e: 5400 RPM is standard for consumer drives. 7200 RPM is for performance desktops, and 10,000 RPM+ is enterprise.

questions.q: Which form factor is standard for desktop hard drives?
questions.e: 3.5-inch is desktop size. 2.5-inch is laptop and external drive size.

questions.q: Which storage interface is enterprise-grade, faster than SATA and typically used in servers and data centres?
questions.e: Serial Attached SCSI is the server and data centre interface. SATA III tops out at 6 Gbps; your notes give SAS as 12 Gbps (newer SAS versions go higher).

questions.q: What is the maximum transfer rate of SATA III?
questions.e: SATA III is 6 Gbps, roughly 600 MB/s. 7,000 MB/s is the sort of speed a PCIe 4.0 NVMe drive reaches.

questions.q: An M.2 slot can take which kinds of SSD?
o: Both SATA-based and NVMe (PCIe) M.2 drives, depending on the slot
questions.e: M.2 is just a form factor. M.2 SSDs come in SATA (limited to 6 Gbps) and NVMe (PCIe) versions, so check what the slot supports.

questions.q: What do SATA data and power connectors look like?
questions.e: SATA uses a 7-pin L-shaped data connector and a 15-pin power connector.

questions.q: What capacity is a single-layer DVD?
questions.e: Single-layer DVD is 4.7 GB, dual-layer is 8.5 GB. CDs hold about 700 MB, and Blu-ray goes up to 100 GB on triple-layer discs.

questions.q: Which technology do SSDs and flash drives use to store data?
questions.e: SSDs use non-volatile NAND flash, giving speed, durability and lower power use. HDDs use magnetic platters, and optical discs use lasers.

questions.q: Which connection gives external drives SATA-level speed and is described as faster than USB 3.0?
questions.e: eSATA is SATA for external enclosures, up to 6 Gbps.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of drives for RAID 5?
questions.e: RAID 5 (striping with parity) needs at least 3 drives and survives one drive failure.

questions.q: Which RAID level gives the best performance but no fault tolerance at all?
questions.e: RAID 0 stripes data across drives for speed. If any single drive fails, everything is lost.

questions.q: Which RAID level mirrors data so an exact copy exists on a second drive?
questions.e: RAID 1 is mirroring: minimum 2 drives, survives one failure, good for boot drives and critical data.

questions.q: A data centre needs an array that can survive two drives failing at the same time. Which RAID level should they use?
questions.e: RAID 6 uses double parity, needs at least 4 drives and survives two simultaneous failures.

questions.q: Which RAID level combines striping and mirroring and needs at least 4 drives?
questions.e: RAID 10 stripes across mirrored pairs, giving both speed and redundancy. It survives multiple failures as long as no mirrored pair loses both drives.

questions.q: A video studio wants maximum read/write speed for scratch storage and accepts that one drive failure will lose everything. Which RAID level?
questions.e: RAID 0 gives the best speed with no redundancy, which the studio has accepted.

questions.q: What size is a standard ATX motherboard?
questions.e: ATX is 12 x 9.6 in. microATX is 9.6 x 9.6 in, Mini-ITX 6.7 x 6.7 in and Pico-ITX 3.9 x 2.8 in.

questions.q: Which form factor is square, 9.6 x 9.6 inches, with around 4 expansion slots, and is popular for budget office PCs?
questions.e: microATX balances size and expandability, typically with 4 slots and 2 to 4 DIMM slots.

questions.q: A customer wants a tiny living room PC (HTPC) with one graphics card slot. Which form factor fits?
questions.e: Mini-ITX (170 x 170 mm) usually has one PCIe slot and two DIMM slots, ideal for small builds. Pico-ITX is for embedded/IoT and has no room for a GPU.

questions.q: Which form factor would you expect in an embedded industrial IoT device?
questions.e: Pico-ITX (100 x 72 mm) is tiny and low power, suiting embedded systems.

questions.q: Which expansion slot is the legacy one that PCIe replaced?
questions.e: PCI is the old parallel expansion slot (133 to 533 MB/s). PCIe replaced it with serial lanes (x1, x4, x8, x16).

questions.q: Roughly how much bandwidth does each PCIe 4.0 lane provide?
questions.e: Each generation doubles: PCIe 3.0 is about 1 GB/s per lane, 4.0 about 2 GB/s, 5.0 about 4 GB/s. A x16 PCIe 4.0 slot gives about 32 GB/s.

questions.q: Which connector supplies extra power directly to a dedicated graphics card?
questions.e: GPUs draw extra power through 6-pin, 8-pin or 6+2-pin PCIe power connectors.

questions.q: A newly built PC won't power on at all. Which motherboard connector should you check first?
questions.e: The 24-pin is the motherboard's main power. Without it the system won't start. Also check the front-panel header, since the power button connects there.

questions.q: What connects the case's power button, reset button and LEDs to the motherboard?
questions.e: Headers are small pin connectors for case features: front panel, USB, fan and audio headers.

questions.q: Which SAN protocol carries storage traffic over ordinary TCP/IP networks?
questions.e: iSCSI runs over TCP/IP. Fibre Channel is a dedicated high-speed storage network technology (up to 128 Gbps).

questions.q: Which is a feature of UEFI but not legacy BIOS?
o: Support for GPT boot drives larger than 2 TB
questions.e: UEFI supports GPT (boot drives over 2 TB), Secure Boot, faster boot and mouse support. Legacy BIOS is 16-bit, keyboard-only and limited to MBR.

questions.q: What does Secure Boot do?
o: Checks bootloader digital signatures so only trusted OS code loads at startup
Requires a password before the OS loads
questions.e: Secure Boot verifies the signatures of bootloaders, blocking unauthorised OSs and boot-level malware like rootkits.

questions.q: Which TPM version is required to install Windows 11?
questions.e: Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0. TPM is a hardware security module used by features like BitLocker.

questions.q: A school wants to stop students changing boot settings in the firmware. What should IT set?
questions.e: The administrator password locks the setup utility. A user/boot password only stops the system booting without it.

questions.q: A company wants to stop anyone booting company PCs from a USB stick. Which firmware setting helps?
o: Disable USB boot (USB permissions) in BIOS/UEFI
questions.e: USB permissions in firmware control whether the system can boot from or access USB devices.

questions.q: What does PWM fan mode do?
o: Lets the motherboard adjust fan speed dynamically based on temperature
Runs the fan at a fixed voltage
questions.e: Pulse Width Modulation varies fan speed according to temperature. DC mode uses fixed voltage regulation.

questions.q: What is the maximum RAM a 32-bit CPU can address?
questions.e: 2 to the power of 32 gives 4 GB of address space. 64-bit CPUs can address vastly more (up to 18 exabytes in theory).

questions.q: What is Intel's version of simultaneous multithreading called?
questions.e: Hyper-Threading is Intel's name. AMD calls it SMT (Simultaneous Multithreading). VT-x is Intel's virtualisation extension.

questions.q: A developer can't start virtual machines on their PC. What should be enabled in the BIOS/UEFI?
o: Intel VT-x or AMD-V hardware virtualisation
questions.e: Hypervisors like Hyper-V, VMware and VirtualBox need hardware-assisted virtualisation (VT-x/AMD-V), which is often disabled by default.

questions.q: A customer is upgrading from a 10th-gen Intel Core CPU to a 13th-gen one. What must they check?
o: The motherboard socket, because 10th gen uses LGA 1200 and 12th/13th gen uses LGA 1700
questions.e: CPU and motherboard socket must match. Per the notes, 10th gen is LGA 1200 and 12th/13th gen is LGA 1700, so a new motherboard is needed.

questions.q: Which AMD socket is used by the Ryzen 7000 series?
questions.e: AM5 is Ryzen 7000. AM4 covers Ryzen 1000 to 5000, and SP5 is for EPYC server CPUs.

questions.q: What is needed to overclock a CPU?
o: An unlocked CPU (e.g. Intel K series) and better cooling
questions.e: Overclocking pushes clock speed beyond factory settings. It needs an unlocked CPU and produces more heat, so cooling must be improved.

questions.q: Which slot does a modern graphics card normally use?
questions.e: GPUs use PCIe x16. Sound cards and basic NICs often use x1, and capture cards often use x4.

questions.q: A streamer wants to record 4K console gameplay with zero-latency HDMI pass-through. Which expansion card do they need?
questions.e: Capture cards record or stream video from external sources, often with HDMI pass-through and hardware encoding.

questions.q: Which card manages multiple drives as RAID arrays and may include battery-backed cache?
questions.e: RAID controller cards manage RAID levels (0, 1, 5, 6, 10 and more). Cache with battery backup protects data during power loss.

questions.q: A music producer needs 192 kHz/24-bit recording with optical (TOSLINK) output. Which upgrade should they install?
questions.e: Sound cards improve audio beyond onboard sound, with higher sample rates and connectors like TOSLINK and RCA.

questions.q: What does a CFM rating on a fan measure?
o: The volume of air it moves per minute
questions.e: Cubic feet per minute measures airflow. Higher CFM means more cooling, but usually more noise. Fan speed is measured in RPM.

questions.q: What is the most common case fan size?
questions.e: 120mm balances airflow and noise. 80mm is for compact cases, and 240mm usually refers to radiator size in liquid cooling.

questions.q: What does thermal paste do?
o: Fills microscopic gaps between the CPU and heat sink to improve heat transfer
Glues the heat sink to the motherboard
questions.e: Thermal paste (thermal interface material) removes air pockets between the CPU/GPU and cooler. Without it, the CPU overheats.

questions.q: What should you use to clean old thermal paste off a CPU before re-applying?
o: Isopropyl alcohol (90% or higher) and a lint-free cloth
questions.e: High-percentage isopropyl alcohol and a lint-free cloth remove old paste safely.

questions.q: In a liquid cooling system, which part transfers heat from the coolant to the air?
questions.e: The water block absorbs heat from the CPU/GPU, the pump circulates coolant, and the radiator (with its fans) releases the heat into the air.

questions.q: What is passive cooling?
o: Heat sinks with no moving parts, relying on metal fins
A fan mounted on a heat sink
A PSU fan running at full speed
questions.e: Passive cooling has no fans: just heat sinks. It's common for chipsets, embedded systems and low-power CPUs. Active cooling adds a fan.

questions.q: Which PSU voltage rail powers the CPU, GPU, fans and mechanical hard drives?
questions.e: +12V powers the hungriest components. +5V covers USB and legacy devices, and +3.3V powers RAM, PCIe cards and chipsets.

questions.q: What is the standard mains voltage in the UK and Europe?
questions.e: Europe uses 220 to 240 V AC at 50 Hz. North America and Japan use 110 to 120 V. Older PSUs may have a manual voltage switch; modern ones auto-switch.

questions.q: What is the advantage of a fully modular PSU?
o: You only connect the cables you need, improving cable management and airflow
It provides backup power if the PSU fails
questions.e: Modular PSUs have detachable cables. Semi-modular have fixed motherboard cables and detachable peripheral cables. Non-modular have everything fixed.

questions.q: A critical server must keep running even if a power supply fails, and the failed unit must be replaceable without shutting down. What should be installed?
questions.e: Redundant power supplies provide backup on PSU failure, and hot-swappable modules can be replaced while running.

questions.q: Which 80 PLUS rating is the most efficient?
questions.e: Order from lowest to highest: Standard, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Titanium (about 94%).

questions.q: Why is the main motherboard power connector described as 20+4 pin?
o: The extra 4 pins detach so it fits older 20-pin boards as well as modern 24-pin boards
It has 20 pins for the CPU and 4 for the GPU
It splits into two SATA connectors
questions.e: Older boards used 20 pins; modern boards use 24. The detachable 4-pin section makes one connector work with both.

questions.q: What formula calculates wattage?
questions.e: Power (W) = voltage (V) x current (A). Online PSU calculators add up the needs of each component.

questions.q: Which printer language was developed by Adobe and is preferred for graphics and publishing?
questions.e: PostScript (Adobe) gives precise rendering for design work. PCL (HP) is faster and widely used for general business printing.

questions.q: A hospital wants print jobs held at the printer until the user arrives and authenticates. Which feature is this?
questions.e: Secured printing holds jobs until the user releases them at the device, often with a PIN or badge. Audit logs track who printed what.

questions.q: Users want an MFD to scan documents straight into a shared network folder. Which scan service should be configured?
questions.e: SMB scanning saves to a network share. Other options are scan to email and scan to cloud services.

questions.q: Which scanner part lets you scan a stack of loose pages in one batch?
questions.e: An ADF feeds multiple pages automatically. Flatbeds are for single, delicate, bound or oversized documents.

questions.q: What is the difference between a printer share and a print server?
o: A printer share is a printer on one PC shared via its OS; a print server is a dedicated device or software managing queues for many printers
A print server is only for USB printers
A printer share needs a domain controller
questions.e: Printer sharing is fine for small setups. Print servers centralise queues and management for larger offices.

questions.q: Why should you keep a printer's firmware updated?
o: It fixes bugs and security vulnerabilities and can add features
It's needed for duplex printing to work at all
It changes the printer language from PCL to PostScript
questions.e: Firmware updates fix bugs and patch security issues, and can add features such as cloud printing.

questions.q: What does a laser printer maintenance kit usually include?
o: A new fuser assembly, rollers and separation pads
Thermal paper and a cleaning pen
questions.e: Laser maintenance kits replace worn parts like the fuser and rollers. After fitting one, reset the maintenance counter.

questions.q: An inkjet printer produces streaky, faded prints with missing lines. What should you try first?
questions.e: Clogged inkjet nozzles cause streaks. The built-in cleaning cycle is the first step; manual cleaning with isopropyl alcohol is next.

questions.q: Which printer type needs special heat-sensitive paper?
questions.e: Thermal printers (receipts, labels) use chemically coated paper that darkens with heat. Maintenance includes cleaning the heating element.

questions.q: A bank needs to print carbon copies on multipart forms. Which printer type is used?
questions.e: Impact printers physically strike an inked ribbon against the paper, so they can produce copies through multipart paper. Maintenance means replacing ribbon, printhead and paper.

questions.q: What should you use to clean a thermal printer's printhead?
o: A thermal cleaning pen or isopropyl alcohol on a lint-free cloth
questions.e: The notes specify a thermal cleaning pen or isopropyl alcohol on a lint-free cloth. Debris in the feed assembly is cleared with compressed air or a soft brush.

questions.q: A PC keeps losing its date and time every time it's unplugged. What is the most likely fix?
questions.e: A dead CMOS battery means the firmware can't keep the clock and settings when mains power is removed.
questions.l: Troubleshooting motherboards, RAM, CPUs and power

questions.q: A PC powers on but beeps several times and doesn't boot. Where do you look to decode the beeps?
questions.e: POST beep codes vary by manufacturer and point to issues like RAM, CPU or GPU problems. Look them up in the motherboard documentation.
questions.l: Troubleshooting motherboards, RAM, CPUs and power

questions.q: You notice bulging, leaking capacitors on a motherboard. What should you do?
o: Replace the motherboard, and consider a UPS to protect against surges
questions.e: Swollen capacitors come from age or power surges. The board (or PSU, if that's where they are) needs replacing.
questions.l: Troubleshooting motherboards, RAM, CPUs and power

questions.q: A PC gives frequent blue screens and app crashes. Which tool helps you test whether RAM is faulty?
questions.e: Memory errors cause crashes and BSODs. Windows Memory Diagnostic and MemTest86 test RAM. CHKDSK checks disks.
questions.l: Troubleshooting motherboards, RAM, CPUs and power

questions.q: A strong burning smell is coming from a running PC. What is the first thing to do?
o: Power it off immediately and inspect for burnt components
Open the case while it runs to find the smell
questions.e: Burning smells suggest a short circuit, overloaded PSU or failing capacitors. Power off straight away for safety.
questions.l: Troubleshooting motherboards, RAM, CPUs and power

questions.q: A workstation shuts off randomly under heavy load. Which two areas should you check first?
questions.e: Random shutdowns usually come from overheating (triggering a protective shutdown) or a failing PSU with fluctuating voltages. Faulty RAM is another possibility.
questions.l: Troubleshooting motherboards, RAM, CPUs and power

questions.q: A PC is completely dead: no fans, lights or beeps. Which is the most useful first check?
o: Confirm the outlet works, then check the PSU and its 24-pin and CPU power connections
questions.e: With no power at all, start with power: the outlet, the PSU (multimeter or known-good swap) and the motherboard power cables.
questions.l: Troubleshooting motherboards, RAM, CPUs and power

questions.q: An HDD makes a repetitive clicking noise. What should you do first?
o: Back up critical data immediately, then replace the drive
questions.e: Clicking usually means a failing read/write head or actuator, so failure is close. Get the data off first.

questions.q: What does S.M.A.R.T. do?
o: Monitors drive health and warns of failure before it happens
questions.e: Self-Monitoring, Analysis and Reporting Technology tracks things like reallocated sectors. If it reports a failure, replace the drive before it dies.

questions.q: Which maintenance task should NOT be done on an SSD?
questions.e: Defragmenting helps HDDs but just adds needless writes to SSDs. For SSDs, keep TRIM enabled and firmware up to date.

questions.q: A new NVMe SSD is installed but doesn't appear in File Explorer. What should you do?
o: Initialise and format it in Disk Management
questions.e: A new drive needs initialising and partitioning before Windows shows it. Disk Management (Windows) or GParted (Linux) handles this. Also check cables/seating and BIOS.

questions.q: A server's RAID 5 array shows one failed drive and is running degraded. What is the correct action?
o: Replace the failed drive and let the controller rebuild the array
Convert it to RAID 0 for speed
Ignore it, as RAID 5 has no redundancy anyway
questions.e: Replace the failed drive and follow the rebuild procedure. Never reinitialise an array unless data is backed up, as that wipes it.

questions.q: On boot a PC says 'bootable device not found'. Which is a sensible first check?
o: The boot order in BIOS/UEFI and whether the drive is detected
questions.e: Causes include a disconnected or failed drive, wrong boot order or corrupt boot files. Check firmware settings first, then use boot repair tools.

questions.q: Which command checks a Windows drive for file system errors and bad sectors?
questions.e: CHKDSK is the Windows tool. fsck is the Linux equivalent.

questions.q: A new monitor shows 'No Signal' even though it's on and the PC is running. What should you check first?
o: The input source selected on the monitor
questions.e: An incorrect input source is the classic cause. Select the right input (HDMI, DisplayPort and so on) in the monitor's menu, then check the cable.

questions.q: A faint ghost of a taskbar stays visible on an OLED screen. What is this called?
questions.e: Burn-in comes from static images displayed for a long time, especially on OLED and plasma. Screen savers, pixel refresh and auto-dimming help prevent it.

questions.q: The image on a monitor looks blurry and text is fuzzy. What is the most likely cause?
o: The resolution isn't set to the monitor's native resolution
The refresh rate is too high
questions.e: LCDs look sharpest at their native resolution. For projectors, a dirty lens or poor focus also causes fuzziness.

questions.q: A meeting room projector gets dimmer over months and now barely shows an image. What is most likely needed?
questions.e: Projector bulbs last roughly 2,000 to 6,000 hours and dim with age. Check the lamp indicator and replace it.

questions.q: A projector keeps shutting itself off after about 30 minutes of use. What should you check?
o: Dust in the vents and filters causing overheating
questions.e: Intermittent shutdown is usually overheating from blocked vents or filters. Clean them and check the fan.

questions.q: A laptop connected to a TV by HDMI plays video but the sound still comes from the laptop speakers. What should you change?
o: Set the HDMI device as the default playback device in Windows sound settings
Replace the HDMI cable with VGA
questions.e: HDMI carries audio, but Windows must be told to use it. Choose the right playback device in Sound settings. VGA carries no audio at all.

questions.q: The picture on a projector is cut off at the edges. Which settings should you look at?
o: Display scaling in the OS and overscan on the projector
questions.e: Sizing problems come from scaling settings or overscan/underscan. Adjust scaling and disable overscan.

questions.q: A second monitor suddenly has a green tint. What is a likely cause?
o: A loose or damaged video cable
questions.e: Incorrect colours often come from a damaged cable or connector, or from misconfigured colour settings. Try a known-good cable or a different port.

questions.q: Prints from a laser printer show a faint duplicate of the text further down the page. What is this, and what is the likely cause?
o: Echo/ghost images, usually from the fuser or a worn transfer roller
Garbled print from a bad driver
questions.e: Double or echo images point to the fuser not heating the toner properly or a worn transfer roller.

questions.q: A printer outputs pages of random symbols and nonsense characters. What is the most likely fix?
o: Reinstall the correct printer driver and restart the print spooler
questions.e: Garbled output means the computer is sending data the printer doesn't understand: wrong or corrupt drivers, or a spooler problem.

questions.q: Print jobs are stuck in the queue and nothing will print. What should you do?
o: Restart the Print Spooler service and clear the queue
questions.e: A frozen queue usually means a stuck spooler or corrupt job. Restart the spooler (services.msc), or use net stop spooler, delete the files in the spool PRINTERS folder, then net start spooler.

questions.q: A printer keeps pulling several sheets at once. What is the likely cause and fix?
o: Worn pickup rollers or damp paper; replace the rollers and use fresh paper, fanning the stack
A full queue; restart the spooler
questions.e: Multipage misfeeds come from worn pickup rollers that no longer separate sheets, or humidity making sheets stick together.

questions.q: A network printer keeps disappearing for users after it's been power-cycled. What is a good fix?
o: Give the printer a static IP or DHCP reservation
questions.e: If the printer's address changes, clients lose it. A static IP (or reservation) keeps it consistent and avoids IP conflicts.

questions.q: Vertical lines run down every page from a laser printer. What is the likely cause?
o: A dirty or damaged imaging drum
questions.e: On laser printers, lines usually mean a dirty or damaged drum. On inkjets the equivalent cause is clogged nozzles.

questions.q: Prints from a laser printer are faint and hard to read. What should you check?
o: Toner level and whether EconoMode/low-quality settings are on
questions.e: Faded prints come from low toner/ink or economy settings. Replace the cartridge or change to a higher-quality mode.

questions.q: Which Windows edition is the first (lowest) to include BitLocker, domain join and Remote Desktop hosting?
questions.e: Home lacks BitLocker, domain join, Group Policy and RDP hosting. Pro adds them all, and Enterprise adds features such as Autopilot and LTSC on top.

questions.q: Which file extension is used by Debian-based Linux distributions such as Ubuntu for software packages?
questions.e: .deb is Debian/Ubuntu/Mint. .rpm is Red Hat, Fedora and CentOS. .msi is a Windows installer and .dmg is macOS.

questions.q: Which OS is a lightweight, Linux-based system from Google that relies heavily on web apps and cloud storage?
questions.e: ChromeOS runs on Chromebooks, uses web apps (PWAs) and can run Android (.apk) and Linux apps. It's popular in schools.

questions.q: A Mac user needs to run a Windows-only application. What is a common solution?
o: Run Windows in a virtual machine such as Parallels or VMware Fusion
Format the Mac's drive as NTFS
Install the app from the Mac App Store
questions.e: Windows applications don't run natively on macOS. A VM (or a compatibility layer) is the usual answer.

questions.q: Which Linux distribution is designed specifically for penetration testing and security work?
questions.e: Kali comes loaded with security testing tools. RHEL is the commercial, business-supported distro, and Ubuntu is the beginner-friendly one.

questions.q: What is the maximum single file size on FAT32?
questions.e: FAT32 limits files to 4 GB (and partitions to 2 TB). That's why a large video file won't copy to a FAT32 USB stick.

questions.q: A user needs a USB drive that works on both Windows and macOS and can hold an 8 GB video file. Which file system should you use?
questions.e: exFAT supports huge files and is readable and writable on both Windows and macOS. FAT32 caps files at 4 GB; NTFS and APFS each favour their own OS.

questions.q: Which is the default file system for most Linux distributions?
questions.e: ext4 is the Linux default, with journaling and support for large files. XFS is used for high-performance enterprise workloads.

questions.q: Which Windows file system offers self-healing (automatic correction of corrupted data) and is designed for servers and Storage Spaces?
questions.e: ReFS (Resilient File System) is built for resilience and large-scale storage. NTFS remains the standard Windows file system with permissions and encryption.

questions.q: Which file system feature lets NTFS set permissions on individual files and folders?
questions.e: ACLs provide NTFS permissions. Journaling helps recover after crashes. Snapshots are an APFS feature.

questions.q: Which file system is Apple's default on modern Macs, iPhones and iPads, optimised for SSDs and supporting snapshots?
questions.e: APFS replaced HFS+ and is designed for flash storage, with snapshots, cloning and strong encryption.

questions.q: A company needs to install the same configured Windows build, with apps, on 50 identical laptops. Which installation type is most efficient?
questions.e: Image deployment pushes a pre-configured image to many machines, using tools like WDS, MDT or Clonezilla.

questions.q: New employee laptops ship straight to staff and set themselves up with corporate settings with no IT involvement. What is this?
questions.e: Zero-touch deployment is fully automated, using tools like Intune, SCCM or Autopilot.

questions.q: Which installation reinstalls Windows to fix corrupted system files while keeping the user's files and apps?
