questions.e: Corporate-owned devices can be fully managed. BYOD needs profile security requirements and policies that protect company data without overreaching into personal data.
questions.l: Securing mobile devices (not in your notes)

questions.q: Why is device encryption important on phones and tablets?
o: It protects stored data if the device is lost or stolen
It makes the battery last longer
It is only needed on Android
questions.e: Device encryption protects data at rest. Modern iOS and Android encrypt by default once a passcode is set.
questions.l: Securing mobile devices (not in your notes)

questions.q: Which practice keeps a phone protected against newly discovered vulnerabilities?
o: Keeping the OS and apps updated (patch management)
questions.e: Patch management (OS and app updates) is a core mobile hardening practice, along with endpoint security software.
questions.l: Securing mobile devices (not in your notes)

questions.q: A PC gets a blue screen after a new graphics driver was installed. What is a sensible first fix?
o: Boot into Safe Mode and roll back the driver
questions.e: BSODs after a change point to that change. Roll back the driver or update, or use System Restore.
questions.l: Windows OS troubleshooting (not in your notes)

questions.q: A user's profile takes several minutes to load at sign-in, while other users on the same PC are fine. What is a common fix?
questions.e: Slow profile load affecting one user usually means a corrupt or bloated profile. Rebuild it (back up the user's data first).
questions.l: Windows OS troubleshooting (not in your notes)

questions.q: A Windows update causes an important app to stop working. What can you do?
questions.e: Rolling back updates is one of the listed solutions for Windows OS issues.
questions.l: Windows OS troubleshooting (not in your notes)

questions.q: A PC's clock keeps drifting several minutes out over time, causing sign-in problems on the domain. What is the likely cause and fix?
o: Time drift; sync with an NTP time source (and check the CMOS battery)
questions.e: Time drift breaks Kerberos authentication, which needs clocks to match closely. Sync to a time server and check the CMOS battery.
questions.l: Windows OS troubleshooting (not in your notes)

questions.q: A Windows service fails to start at boot. What should you try first?
o: Check the service in services.msc and Event Viewer, then restart it
questions.e: Restarting services and checking logs for the reason are the first steps.
questions.l: Windows OS troubleshooting (not in your notes)

questions.q: Windows shows frequent 'low memory' warnings when several apps are open. Which is the best long-term fix?
o: Add more RAM (increase resources) or close unneeded apps
questions.e: Low memory warnings mean the system needs more resources. Also check that the system meets app requirements.
questions.l: Windows OS troubleshooting (not in your notes)

questions.q: A PC says 'no operating system found' even though the drive is detected in the BIOS. Which is a reasonable step?
o: Use Windows recovery tools to repair the boot configuration
questions.e: If the drive is present but there's no bootable OS, the boot configuration is likely corrupt. Startup repair or boot repair tools fix this, and reimaging is the last resort.
questions.l: Windows OS troubleshooting (not in your notes)

questions.q: Windows is unstable after corrupted system files were found. Which command repairs protected system files?
questions.e: System File Checker repairs system files. If that fails, repair-install Windows, use System Restore or reimage.
questions.l: Windows OS troubleshooting (not in your notes)

questions.q: What does a laptop docking station usually offer that a basic port replicator doesn't?
o: Extra capability such as charging the laptop and expansion like drive bays or PCIe slots
A replacement battery for the laptop
A built-in Wi-Fi access point for the whole office
questions.e: A port replicator just copies the laptop's ports onto a desk unit. A docking station can add charging, extra expansion and a one-connection desk setup.

questions.q: A user wants wireless earbuds that connect straight to their phone with no cable or dongle. Which connection method do they use?
questions.e: Wireless earbuds and headsets connect over Bluetooth. NFC is only used by some models to start pairing with a tap.

questions.q: Which connector do the latest iPhones use for charging and data?
questions.e: Apple moved iPhones from Lightning to USB-C from the iPhone 15 onwards. Older iPhones still use Lightning.

questions.q: A laptop user without a touchscreen wants to sketch diagrams precisely with a pen. Which accessory fits best?
questions.e: A drawing pad gives pressure-sensitive pen input on devices that don't have a touchscreen.

questions.q: A passenger needs to turn off every wireless radio on their phone before take-off. What is the quickest way?
questions.e: Airplane mode disables cellular, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth in one go. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth can be turned back on individually if the airline allows.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: Which mobile network generation offers the highest speeds and lowest latency?
questions.e: 5G is the newest cellular generation, with the fastest speeds and lowest latency. 4G LTE is still widely used as a fallback.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: A user travelling abroad wants to avoid surprise mobile data charges but still use hotel Wi-Fi. What should they turn off?
questions.e: Turning off data roaming stops the phone using foreign networks for data while leaving Wi-Fi available.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: When pairing two Bluetooth devices, what does a matching PIN or passkey on both screens confirm?
o: That both devices are connecting to each other and not to an impostor
That the battery is fully charged
That the devices are on the same Wi-Fi network
That the phone has an eSIM
questions.e: Comparing or entering a passkey during pairing makes sure the right two devices are being paired.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: A delivery app keeps tracking a user's location even when it's closed. How can the user limit this?
o: Change the app's location permission to 'only while using the app'
Uninstall the phone's operating system updates
questions.e: Both iOS and Android let users set location access per app: always, while using, ask each time or never.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: What is a trade-off of using a wide 160 MHz channel on Wi-Fi?
o: Faster throughput, but fewer non-overlapping channels and more chance of interference
It only works on the 2.4 GHz band
questions.e: Wider channels carry more data, but they use up more of the band, so there are fewer clean channels for neighbouring networks.

questions.q: A home's 5 GHz Wi-Fi is fast near the router but drops in the back bedroom, while 2.4 GHz still works there. Why?
o: 5 GHz has a shorter range and is weakened more by walls
5 GHz only works with Wi-Fi 4 devices
The 2.4 GHz band has more channels
questions.e: Higher frequencies give faster speeds but don't travel as far or pass through walls as well. 2.4 GHz reaches further but is slower and more crowded.

questions.q: Which internet appliance filters junk and malicious email before it reaches users' inboxes?
questions.e: A spam gateway sits in front of the mail server and filters unsolicited and malicious email.

questions.q: Which server role lets staff store files centrally and open them from any PC on the network?
questions.e: A file server provides shared storage. Permissions control who can read or change each folder.

questions.q: Why should smart TVs, cameras and other IoT devices be kept on their own network segment?
o: They are often poorly secured, so isolating them limits the damage if one is compromised
They need more bandwidth than PCs
They only work on wired networks
questions.e: IoT devices often have weak default settings and rare updates. A separate VLAN or guest network stops an attacker using one to reach business systems.

questions.q: In AAA, which part records what a user did and when?
questions.e: Authentication proves who you are, authorisation decides what you can do, and accounting logs what you did.

questions.q: A factory relies on an old embedded control system that can no longer be patched. What is the best way to reduce the risk?
o: Isolate it from the main network with a separate segment and strict firewall rules
Connect it directly to the internet for remote support
Install a game on it to test performance
Give all staff the admin password
questions.e: Legacy and embedded systems that can't be updated should be isolated (air-gapped or tightly segmented) so attackers can't reach them.

questions.q: What is software-defined networking (SDN)?
o: Controlling the network centrally through software, separate from the hardware that forwards traffic
Software that only runs on unmanaged switches
questions.e: SDN separates the control plane (decisions, made centrally in software) from the data plane (the devices moving the traffic).

questions.q: Which device allows or blocks traffic entering or leaving a network based on rules?
questions.e: Firewalls filter traffic by rules such as IP address, port and protocol. Anything not allowed is blocked by default.

questions.q: Which device connects a home to the internet over an ordinary telephone line?
questions.e: DSL runs over copper phone lines. Cable modems use coax (DOCSIS) and ONTs terminate fibre.

questions.q: What does the default gateway setting on a PC do?
o: Gives the router address the PC sends traffic to when it's going to another network
Assigns IP addresses to other PCs
questions.e: Traffic for anywhere outside the local subnet goes to the default gateway, usually the router.

questions.q: What is the IPv6 loopback address?
questions.e: ::1 is the IPv6 loopback, the same idea as 127.0.0.1 in IPv4. fe80:: addresses are link-local.

questions.q: How can many home devices with private IP addresses share one public IP address on the internet?
o: The router uses NAT (Network Address Translation)
The ISP gives every device its own public address
DNS merges them into one name
questions.e: NAT on the router translates private internal addresses to the single public address the ISP provides.

questions.q: Which tool removes a cable's outer jacket without damaging the wires inside?
questions.e: A cable stripper cuts just the outer sheath so the twisted pairs can be prepared for termination.

questions.q: A cable tester shows two wires are crossed on one end of a new patch cable. What needs doing?
o: Cut off the plug and re-terminate it in the correct pinout
Use a loopback plug to fix it
questions.e: Crossed or swapped pairs mean the plug was crimped in the wrong order. Re-terminate using T568A or T568B consistently.

questions.q: In a toner probe kit, what do you connect to the known end of the cable?
questions.e: The tone generator puts a signal on the cable at one end, and the probe picks up that tone to find the other end.

questions.q: Why use a punchdown tool rather than a screwdriver on a keystone jack?
o: It seats each wire properly and trims the excess in one action
questions.e: A punchdown tool pushes the wire into the IDC contacts and cuts the spare end, giving a reliable connection.

questions.q: Which tool shows nearby Wi-Fi networks, the channels they use and their signal strength?
questions.e: A Wi-Fi analyser helps choose a clear channel and find dead spots and interference.

questions.q: Before crimping an RJ-45 plug, what must you do?
o: Arrange the wires in the correct order and push them fully into the plug
Test the cable with a loopback plug
Connect it to a PoE switch
Punch the wires down on a patch panel
questions.e: The wires must be in T568A or T568B order and reach the end of the plug, or the crimp will give a bad connection.

questions.q: Which aspect ratio do most modern widescreen monitors and TVs use?
questions.e: 16:9 is the standard widescreen ratio. 4:3 was common on older monitors, and 21:9 is ultrawide.

questions.q: Which display type needs a backlight to show an image?
questions.e: LCD panels (IPS, TN, VA) need a backlight, now usually LED. OLED pixels produce their own light.

questions.q: What is virtual memory?
o: Space on the drive (the page file) used as an overflow when RAM is full
Extra RAM built into the CPU
Memory used only by virtual machines
RAM that corrects its own errors
questions.e: When physical RAM runs out, Windows moves less-used data to the page file. It's much slower than real RAM.

questions.q: A PC with 8 GB of RAM becomes very slow when many apps are open, and the drive light is constantly busy. What is the best fix?
questions.e: Constant drive activity when RAM is full means the PC is relying on virtual memory. More RAM removes the bottleneck.

questions.q: What is a key improvement of DDR5 over DDR4?
o: Higher speeds and bandwidth, with two independent sub-channels per module
It uses fewer pins than DDR3
It removes the need for a memory controller
questions.e: DDR5 runs faster and splits each module into two sub-channels. It is keyed differently and won't fit DDR4 slots.

questions.q: A user installs one 3200 MHz stick and one 2666 MHz stick. What usually happens?
o: Both sticks run at the slower 2666 MHz speed
Each stick runs at its own speed
The PC won't boot at all
questions.e: Mixed modules normally run at the speed of the slowest one. Matched modules are best, especially for multichannel.

questions.q: Which memory configuration uses four matched modules together for more bandwidth, common on workstations and servers?
questions.e: Multichannel memory spreads data across several modules at once. Quad-channel uses four.

questions.q: How many pins does a DDR4 SO-DIMM have?
questions.e: Laptop SO-DIMMs: DDR3 204 pins, DDR4 260, DDR5 262. Desktop DDR4 and DDR5 DIMMs both have 288.

questions.q: Before buying RAM for an upgrade, where can you confirm the supported type, maximum capacity and slot order?
o: The motherboard manual or manufacturer's website
questions.e: The motherboard documentation lists the RAM type, speeds, maximum per slot and which slots to fill first.

questions.q: How should you choose the wattage for a new gaming PC's power supply?
o: Add up the power draw of the parts, especially the CPU and GPU, and leave some headroom
Always buy the smallest PSU available
Match the wattage of the monitor
Use the wattage printed on the case
questions.e: Calculate total load and add headroom (often 20 to 30%) so the PSU isn't running at its limit.

questions.q: An older PSU has a manual 115/230 V switch set to 115 V. What happens if it's plugged into UK mains?
o: It is likely to be damaged, as UK mains is around 230 V
questions.e: UK mains is about 230 V. A PSU set to 115 V will get roughly double the voltage it expects and can fail.

questions.q: Which connector powers a modern graphics card directly from the PSU?
questions.e: Graphics cards use PCIe power connectors. High-end cards may use the newer 12V-2x6 (formerly 12VHPWR) connector.

questions.q: Which connector delivers extra power to the CPU on a desktop motherboard?
questions.e: The CPU gets its own 12 V feed near the socket, separate from the 24-pin main connector.

questions.q: What does an auto-switching power supply do?
o: Accepts any mains input from about 100 to 240 V without a manual switch
Switches between two PSUs if one fails
Turns itself off when the PC is idle
Changes its output from DC to AC
questions.e: Auto-switching PSUs detect the input voltage automatically, which suits laptops and travel. Redundant PSUs are a different feature.

questions.q: Why should you download a new printer's driver from the manufacturer's website rather than using the disc in the box?
o: The website has the latest version that supports your OS
The disc driver adds extra toner
questions.e: Drivers on the disc may be out of date or not support the current OS version. The manufacturer's site has the newest release.
questions.l: Extra practice: Printer and MFD setup

questions.q: Users want to scan documents on an MFD and have them emailed to themselves. What must be configured on the MFD?
o: A DHCP reservation for every user
questions.e: Scan to email sends the file through an SMTP server, so the MFD needs the server address, port and any login details.
questions.l: Extra practice: Printer and MFD setup

questions.q: Which printer setting prints on both sides of the page?
questions.e: Duplex prints both sides. Collate keeps multi-page copies in order, and orientation sets portrait or landscape.
questions.l: Extra practice: Printer and MFD setup

questions.q: An office MFD keeps a record of which user printed, scanned or copied what. What is this mainly for?
o: Security and accountability, plus tracking costs
questions.e: Audit logs show who used the device and how. They support security investigations and charging departments for usage.
questions.l: Extra practice: Printer and MFD setup

questions.q: A user needs a spreadsheet printed sideways across the page. Which setting do they change?
questions.e: Page orientation is set in the print dialogue or printer preferences: portrait or landscape.
questions.l: Extra practice: Printer and MFD setup

questions.q: A leased MFD is being returned. Why does its internal storage need wiping first?
o: It may hold copies of scanned and printed documents that could be recovered
It makes the toner last longer
It's needed to reset the paper tray
It speeds up the next owner's printing
questions.e: Many MFDs store jobs on an internal drive. Wiping or removing it protects confidential data.
questions.l: Extra practice: Printer and MFD setup

questions.q: What is the correct order of the laser printing process?
o: Processing, charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, cleaning
Charging, processing, fusing, exposing, developing, transferring, cleaning
Processing, exposing, charging, transferring, developing, cleaning, fusing
Cleaning, charging, developing, exposing, fusing, transferring, processing
questions.e: A memory aid: Please Charge Every Device To Fully Charge (Processing, Charging, Exposing, Developing, Transferring, Fusing, Cleaning).

questions.q: In the laser printing process, which step uses the laser to draw the image onto the drum?
questions.e: During exposing, the laser discharges areas of the drum to form the image. Developing then applies toner to those areas.

questions.q: In the laser printing process, which step applies toner to the drum?
questions.e: Toner sticks to the areas of the drum the laser discharged. Transferring then moves it to the paper.

questions.q: Why should you let a laser printer cool down before replacing the fuser?
o: The fuser gets very hot and can burn you
questions.e: The fuser uses heat (often around 200°C) to melt toner onto the paper. Always power off and let it cool first.

questions.q: After replacing an inkjet cartridge, lines and colours print slightly out of line. What should you do?
questions.e: Inkjet printers include alignment and cleaning utilities. Run them after replacing cartridges.

questions.q: Printouts from a dot matrix printer are getting fainter. What normally needs replacing?
questions.e: Impact printers strike an inked ribbon against the paper, so the ribbon wears out over time.

questions.q: What does a tractor feed do on an impact printer?
o: Pulls continuous paper through using the holes along its edges
questions.e: Tractor feeds use sprockets to grip the perforated edges of continuous-feed paper.

questions.q: Why do virtual machines need patching and antivirus just like physical PCs?
o: Each VM runs its own OS, which has the same vulnerabilities as a physical install
VMs never connect to a network
questions.e: A VM is a full operating system. It needs updates, endpoint protection and the same security controls as real hardware.

questions.q: Before installing a hypervisor on a PC, which firmware setting often needs turning on?
o: Hardware virtualisation support (Intel VT-x or AMD-V)
questions.e: Most hypervisors need the CPU's virtualisation extensions enabled in UEFI/BIOS.

questions.q: What does high availability mean for a cloud service?
o: It keeps running with very little downtime, using redundancy across hardware or sites
Only one user can access it at a time
questions.e: High availability relies on redundant systems so a failure doesn't take the service down.

questions.q: A user edits a document on their laptop and the updated version appears on their phone a minute later. Which cloud feature is this?
questions.e: File sync (OneDrive, Google Drive, iCloud) keeps the same files updated across all of a user's devices.

questions.q: Which cloud deployment model is run by a provider that anyone can sign up to use?
questions.e: Public cloud (Azure, AWS, Google Cloud) is shared infrastructure open to any customer.

questions.q: What is the macOS equivalent of a Windows blue screen of death?
questions.e: A kernel panic is a fatal system error on macOS (and Linux). The pinwheel just means an app is busy.
questions.l: Extra practice: Motherboard, RAM, CPU and power troubleshooting

questions.q: A PC powers on and the fans spin, but there is no picture and no beeps. Which is a sensible check?
o: Reseat the RAM and check the monitor cable and input
questions.e: No video and no POST beeps often points to RAM, the GPU or display connection. Start with the simple, cheap checks.
questions.l: Extra practice: Motherboard, RAM, CPU and power troubleshooting

questions.q: A PC is very slow and its CPU temperature shows 95°C while sitting idle. What is the most likely cause?
o: A cooling problem, such as dust, a failed fan or dried-out thermal paste
questions.e: Some modern CPUs are designed to run near 95°C under full load, but not at idle. Overheating CPUs slow themselves down (throttle), so clean dust, check fans and reapply thermal paste.
questions.l: Extra practice: Motherboard, RAM, CPU and power troubleshooting

questions.q: Straight after a new CPU was installed, the PC overheats and shuts down within minutes. What was most likely missed?
o: Applying thermal paste or seating the cooler properly
questions.e: Without thermal paste and a properly seated cooler, heat can't transfer away from the CPU.
questions.l: Extra practice: Motherboard, RAM, CPU and power troubleshooting

questions.q: A desktop makes a grinding noise from inside the case that changes with fan speed. What is the most likely cause?
questions.e: Grinding that follows fan speed points to a worn fan. A grinding or clicking hard drive is the other common cause.
questions.l: Extra practice: Motherboard, RAM, CPU and power troubleshooting

questions.q: A drive bay LED on a server shows solid amber. What does this usually mean?
o: The drive has a fault and should be checked and replaced
The drive is reading data normally
The drive is the boot drive
questions.e: Amber or red drive LEDs normally signal a fault. Confirm in the management software, then replace the drive.
questions.l: Extra practice: Drive and RAID troubleshooting

questions.q: Copying files to a drive has become very slow, with long read/write times. What should you do first?
o: Check the drive's health with S.M.A.R.T. tools and back up the data
questions.e: Slow read/write times can be an early sign of failure. Protect the data first, then diagnose.
questions.l: Extra practice: Drive and RAID troubleshooting

questions.q: One drive in a RAID 0 array fails. What happens to the data?
o: All of the data on the array is lost
Nothing, as RAID 0 has full redundancy
Only half of each file is lost
questions.e: RAID 0 stripes data with no redundancy. It's fast, but losing any drive loses the whole array.
questions.l: Extra practice: Drive and RAID troubleshooting

questions.q: Which RAID level can survive two drives failing at the same time?
questions.e: RAID 6 uses double parity and needs at least four drives. RAID 5 survives only one failure.
questions.l: Extra practice: Drive and RAID troubleshooting

questions.q: Drives from an old server are moved into a new one, but the RAID array doesn't appear. What is the likely cause?
o: The new RAID controller doesn't have the array configuration yet
The PSU is set to 230 V
questions.e: Arrays are tied to the controller's configuration. Import the foreign config or use a compatible controller.
questions.l: Extra practice: Drive and RAID troubleshooting

questions.q: One pixel on a brand-new monitor always stays black. What is this?
questions.e: A dead pixel never lights. Check the manufacturer's pixel policy, as it may be covered under warranty.
questions.l: Extra practice: Display and projector troubleshooting

questions.q: A monitor's picture flickers constantly. Which checks come first?
o: Reseat the cable and check the refresh rate and graphics driver
questions.e: Loose cables, an unsupported refresh rate or a bad driver are the common causes of flicker.
questions.l: Extra practice: Display and projector troubleshooting

questions.q: A laptop connected to a projector shows its own screen fine, but the projector says 'No signal'. What should you check?
o: The laptop's display mode (duplicate or extend) and the projector's input source
questions.e: Press Windows key + P to choose duplicate or extend, and make sure the projector is set to the right input.
questions.l: Extra practice: Display and projector troubleshooting

questions.q: Colours look wrong across a whole monitor, but the cable has been checked. What should you try next?
o: Check the monitor's colour settings and calibration (or colour profile)
questions.e: Wrong colour settings or a bad colour profile can tint the image. Reset to defaults or recalibrate.
questions.l: Extra practice: Display and projector troubleshooting

questions.q: A phone's battery lasts only a few hours and its battery health shows 70%. What is the fix?
questions.e: Lithium batteries lose capacity over time. Low battery health means the battery itself needs replacing.

questions.q: A laptop's pointer moves on its own without anyone touching the touchpad. What is a likely cause?
o: Cursor drift from a dirty or faulty touchpad or a driver problem
questions.e: Clean the touchpad, update its driver and check its sensitivity settings. Disable it if an external mouse is used.

questions.q: A phone screen is cracked but still displays clearly. Touch doesn't work in one area. Which part has failed?
questions.e: The digitizer is the touch-sensing layer. Damage to it causes dead or erratic touch zones.

questions.q: A phone can't get mobile data, while colleagues' phones work fine in the same spot. What should you try first?
o: Toggle airplane mode and check the SIM and carrier settings
questions.e: Toggling airplane mode forces the phone to reconnect. Then check the SIM is seated and mobile data and APN settings are right.

questions.q: A laptop connects to the office Wi-Fi name but keeps asking for the password and failing. What is the most likely cause?
o: An authentication problem, such as the wrong passphrase or a security type mismatch
questions.e: Repeated password prompts point to authentication: wrong key, expired credentials or the client not supporting the security type.

questions.q: Wi-Fi is slow in a busy office. A Wi-Fi analyser shows many access points on channel 6. What should you do?
o: Move the access point to a less crowded channel or to 5 GHz
questions.e: Channel congestion slows everyone down. Use a clear channel (1, 6 or 11 on 2.4 GHz) or move clients to 5 GHz.

questions.q: One PC has no network connection while everyone else is fine. What should you check first?
o: The network cable and the link lights on the NIC and switch port
The DNS server for the whole office
questions.e: When only one device is affected, start at that device: cable, link lights, NIC and its settings.

questions.q: The internet drops for the whole office at about the same time every evening. What is a sensible next step?
o: Check the router's logs and raise it with the ISP
questions.e: Problems affecting everyone at once point to the router or the ISP line. Logs help show what's dropping and when.

questions.q: A user can reach a website by its IP address but not by its name. What is the likely problem?
questions.e: If the IP works but the name doesn't, name resolution (DNS) is failing. Check DNS settings and flush the cache.

questions.q: Toner smudges and rubs off the page when touched. Which part is most likely at fault?
questions.e: The fuser melts toner onto the paper. If it's not hot enough, toner stays loose.

questions.q: Random small specks of toner appear on laser prints. What is a likely cause?
o: Loose toner inside the printer or a leaking cartridge
questions.e: Speckling comes from stray toner. Clean the printer with a toner vacuum and check the cartridge.

questions.q: Colours on a colour printer look wrong, with reds coming out orange. What should you try?
o: Check the cartridges, run colour calibration and confirm the driver's colour settings
questions.e: Incorrect chroma can come from a low or wrong cartridge, a missed calibration or wrong driver settings.

questions.q: The stapling unit on an MFD keeps jamming. What should you do?
o: Clear the staple jam and refill or replace the staple cartridge following the manufacturer's steps
questions.e: Finishing issues like staple and hole punch jams are fixed at the finisher, following the device's own instructions.

questions.q: A printer makes a loud grinding noise when it pulls in paper. What should you do?
o: Power it off and inspect for obstructions or worn gears and rollers
questions.e: Grinding usually means something is stuck or a mechanical part is worn. Keep using it and it can cause more damage.

questions.q: Which step of the troubleshooting methodology includes 'question the obvious'?
o: Establish a theory of probable cause
questions.e: When forming a theory, start with the simple causes first, such as whether it's plugged in or switched on.

questions.q: Which step of the methodology includes putting preventive measures in place?
o: Verify full system functionality and, if applicable, implement preventive measures
questions.e: Once it's fixed, check everything works and take steps to stop the problem coming back.

questions.q: A user reports three unrelated problems at once. How should you handle them?
o: Fix them all at the same time
questions.e: The methodology says to approach multiple problems individually, so fixes don't get confused.

questions.q: During which step would you refer to the vendor's instructions?
o: Establish a plan of action and implement the solution
questions.e: When planning and carrying out the fix, follow vendor guidance to avoid causing new problems.

questions.q: Before making any change while troubleshooting, what should you always consider?
o: Company policies, procedures and the impact of the change
The colour of the PC case
questions.e: CompTIA's model starts by reminding you to consider corporate policies, procedures and impacts before implementing changes.

questions.q: Which is the lowest Windows 11 edition that can join an Active Directory domain?
questions.e: Home can only join workgroups. Pro, Pro for Workstations, Enterprise and Education can join a domain.

questions.q: A Windows 11 Home user needs BitLocker. What is the simplest legitimate option?
o: Upgrade the edition to Pro with a Pro licence key
Install BitLocker from a third-party website
questions.e: An edition upgrade from Home to Pro unlocks BitLocker, Group Policy Editor and domain join without wiping the PC.

questions.q: Which hardware is required for Windows 11?
o: TPM 2.0 and UEFI firmware with Secure Boot capability
questions.e: Windows 11 needs a compatible 64-bit CPU, 4 GB RAM, 64 GB storage, UEFI with Secure Boot capability and TPM 2.0.

questions.q: Which Windows edition is designed for schools and universities?
questions.e: Education has much the same features as Enterprise, licensed for academic institutions.

questions.q: A video editor wants 256 GB of RAM. Windows 11 Home supports up to 128 GB. What is the lowest edition that would support it?
o: None, as Windows can't use more than 128 GB
questions.e: Pro supports up to 2 TB of RAM. Pro for Workstations and Enterprise support up to 6 TB.

questions.q: Which Windows editions include Hyper-V for running virtual machines?
o: Pro, Enterprise and Education, but not Home
None, as it must be bought separately
questions.e: Hyper-V is included in Pro and above. Home users would need a Type 2 hypervisor such as VirtualBox.

questions.q: Why might a large business choose Windows Enterprise over Pro?
o: Extra security and management features plus volume licensing
It's the only edition that can browse the web
It's the only edition with a Start menu
questions.e: Enterprise adds security and management features such as Credential Guard, plus options like LTSC and volume licensing.

questions.q: A user finds text and icons too small on a high-resolution laptop screen. Where should you change this in Windows 11?
questions.e: Display scaling makes everything larger without lowering the screen resolution.

questions.q: How do you make a network share appear as a drive letter, such as S:, in Windows?
o: Use 'Map network drive' in File Explorer, or the net use command
Use Disk Management to format the share
questions.e: Mapping a drive links a letter to a UNC path like \\server\share and can reconnect at sign-in.

questions.q: Two PCs in a home workgroup can't see each other in File Explorer's Network view. Which setting should be on?
o: Network discovery, on a Private network profile
questions.e: Network discovery lets PCs find each other. It's turned off on Public profiles for security.

questions.q: Where would you set a static IP address on a Windows 11 PC?
o: In the network adapter's IP settings (Settings > Network & internet, or ncpa.cpl)
questions.e: Change IP assignment from Automatic (DHCP) to Manual and enter the IP, subnet mask, gateway and DNS servers.

questions.q: Which macOS feature lets you quickly find files, apps and settings by typing?
questions.e: Spotlight opens with Command + Space and searches the whole Mac.
questions.l: Extra practice: macOS features and tools

questions.q: How do you normally uninstall an app installed from a .dmg file on a Mac?
o: Drag the app from the Applications folder to the Bin
questions.e: Most Mac apps are self-contained .app bundles, so dragging them to the Bin removes them. Some apps include their own uninstaller.
questions.l: Extra practice: macOS features and tools

questions.q: Before installing new software, which OS requirement should you confirm?
o: That the OS version and architecture (32-bit or 64-bit) are supported
That the desktop wallpaper is compatible
questions.e: Check the vendor's supported OS list and architecture before installing.

questions.q: A CAD program needs 4 GB of dedicated video memory. The laptop has integrated graphics that share system RAM. What is the problem?
o: Integrated graphics may not meet the requirement, so a PC with a dedicated GPU is needed
The laptop needs a bigger screen
CAD programs only run on servers
Integrated graphics always have more VRAM
questions.e: Integrated graphics borrow system RAM and are less powerful. Demanding graphics software usually needs a dedicated GPU with its own VRAM.

questions.q: A new app needs 16 GB of RAM, but the office PCs have 8 GB. What should happen before the rollout?
o: Upgrade the RAM or choose different software, as the PCs don't meet the requirements
Install it anyway and hope it runs
Install it on the printer instead
questions.e: Always compare software requirements with the hardware before deploying, or users will get poor performance and crashes.

questions.q: What is an advantage of a downloadable installer over physical media?
o: You get the latest version and don't need a disc drive
It installs without admin rights every time
questions.e: Downloads are usually the newest version. Always get them from the vendor's official site.

questions.q: Which is a 'device impact' to think about before installing new software?
o: It may slow the device, use up storage or conflict with existing drivers or security tools
It affects the office opening hours
questions.e: Device impacts are effects on the machine itself. Network, operational and business impacts are considered too.

questions.q: Which is a 'business impact' of rolling out new software across a company?
o: Staff may need training, and work could be disrupted while people adjust
The PCs' MAC addresses will change
It always speeds up every PC
questions.e: Business impacts include training, productivity dips, licensing costs and whether the software fits existing processes.

questions.q: New PCs arrive with Windows and all company software already included in a prepared build. Which distribution method is this?
questions.e: Image deployment installs the same prepared OS and app build on many machines at once.

questions.q: In OneDrive, what does a cloud icon next to a file mean?
o: The file is stored online only and downloads when you open it
The file is shared with everyone
questions.e: Files On-Demand keeps online-only files in the cloud to save space. A green tick means it's available on the device.

questions.q: Two colleagues need to edit the same report at the same time. Which cloud feature allows this?
o: Real-time co-authoring in a cloud word processor
questions.e: Cloud apps like Word Online and Google Docs let several people edit the same file at once and see each other's changes.

questions.q: A new starter can sign in to email but can't open Teams. What is the most likely cause?
o: No Teams licence has been assigned to their account
questions.e: In Microsoft 365, each app depends on the licences assigned to the user's account.

questions.q: What does identity synchronisation do for cloud productivity tools?
o: Keeps user accounts matched between the company directory and cloud services, so staff use one set of credentials
Copies phone contacts to a laptop
Sets every user's password to the same value
questions.e: Tools like Microsoft Entra Connect sync on-premises Active Directory accounts to the cloud.

questions.q: A user wants their Desktop and Documents folders backed up to OneDrive automatically. Which setting does this?
questions.e: OneDrive's folder backup redirects Desktop, Documents and Pictures to OneDrive so they sync to the cloud.

questions.q: What is a benefit of cloud-based video conferencing over an on-premises system?
o: Staff can join from anywhere and there are no servers to maintain
It only works inside the office
questions.e: Cloud conferencing scales easily and the provider handles maintenance and updates.

questions.q: Files in a user's OneDrive folder show a red cross. What does this mean?
o: They have failed to sync and need checking, such as for a conflict or space problem
questions.e: A red cross means a sync error. Check OneDrive's status for the reason, such as a file name, conflict or storage limit.

questions.q: A member of staff leaves the company. What should happen to their cloud productivity licence?
o: Disable the account, hand over their data, then remove or reassign the licence
Give their password to the whole team
questions.e: Reclaiming licences saves money, and disabling the account first stops them accessing company data.

questions.q: What is the difference between WPA2-Personal and WPA2-Enterprise?
o: Personal uses one shared passphrase; Enterprise checks each user's own credentials through a RADIUS server
questions.e: WPA2-Enterprise uses 802.1X so each person has their own login and access can be removed individually.
questions.l: Extra practice: Wireless security and authentication

questions.q: Which feature of WPA3-Personal makes offline password-guessing attacks much harder?
questions.e: SAE replaces WPA2's pre-shared key handshake, so captured traffic can't be used to guess the password offline.
questions.l: Extra practice: Wireless security and authentication

questions.q: Why is TKIP no longer recommended for Wi-Fi?
o: It's an old, weak encryption method; AES should be used instead
questions.e: TKIP was a stopgap for WPA. It has known weaknesses and is deprecated.
questions.l: Extra practice: Wireless security and authentication

questions.q: Which of these is a true example of multifactor authentication?
o: A password plus a code from an authenticator app
questions.e: MFA needs factors from different categories: something you know, have, are or somewhere you are. A password and PIN are both 'know'.
questions.l: Extra practice: Wireless security and authentication

questions.q: An old office printer only supports WEP for Wi-Fi. What is the best approach?
o: Connect it by cable or replace it, rather than lowering the network's security
Switch the whole network to WEP
questions.e: WEP can be cracked in minutes. Don't weaken the network for one device.
questions.l: Extra practice: Wireless security and authentication

questions.q: In authentication factors, what does 'something you are' refer to?
o: Biometrics, such as a fingerprint or face scan
questions.e: Something you know is a password or PIN, something you have is a token or phone, and something you are is a biometric.
questions.l: Extra practice: Wireless security and authentication

questions.q: What is the final step of the CompTIA malware removal process?
questions.e: The last step is teaching the user how to avoid reinfection, such as spotting phishing and avoiding dodgy downloads.

questions.q: Which step comes straight before 'educate the end user' in the malware removal process?
o: Enable System Restore and create a restore point
questions.e: Once the PC is clean and scans are scheduled, turn System Restore back on and create a clean restore point.

questions.q: Why create a new restore point after malware removal?
o: It gives a clean point to roll back to if something goes wrong later
questions.e: Earlier restore points may contain the malware, so a new clean one is needed.

questions.q: What does quarantining an infected PC involve?
o: Disconnecting it from the network so the malware can't spread
questions.e: Unplug the cable and turn off Wi-Fi to isolate it from other systems.

questions.q: A user says their PC 'has a virus'. What should you do first?
o: Investigate and verify the malware symptoms
questions.e: Step 1 is to confirm it really is malware. Pop-ups, slowness and browser changes can have other causes.

questions.q: Which step of the malware removal process involves updating anti-malware and scanning, using Safe Mode or WinPE if needed?
questions.e: Remediation is where you update definitions and use scan and removal techniques to clean the PC.

questions.q: Why set a UEFI/BIOS password on a workstation?
o: To stop someone changing firmware settings or booting from a USB stick
questions.e: A firmware password protects boot order and security settings like Secure Boot from tampering.

questions.q: A receptionist often leaves their PC unlocked while away from the desk. Which setting helps most?
o: An automatic screen lock after a short period of inactivity
questions.e: A timeout screen lock protects the PC if the user forgets to lock it (Windows key + L).

questions.q: Office staff should only be able to sign in between 8am and 6pm. Which account control does this?
questions.e: Login time restrictions stop accounts being used outside working hours.

questions.q: Why should the Guest account be disabled on workstations?
o: It allows access without proper credentials
It uses too much disk space
questions.e: Disabling guest access makes sure every user must authenticate with their own account.

questions.q: Which password is strongest?
o: A long, unique passphrase such as 'Kettle-Orbit-Gravel-Tango-91'
The same strong password used on every site
questions.e: Length matters most, plus a mix of character types. Every password should be unique.

questions.q: Why turn off services a workstation doesn't need?
o: It stops the user logging in
questions.e: Every running service is a possible way in. Disabling unused ones means fewer targets.

questions.q: Why install a remote backup app on company phones?
o: So data can be restored after the phone is lost, wiped or replaced
questions.e: Remote (cloud) backup means a remote wipe or a lost phone doesn't mean lost data.

questions.q: Which phone screen lock uses 'something you are'?
questions.e: Biometric locks use physical traits. PINs and patterns are things you know.

questions.q: Why install endpoint security software on company Android phones?
o: To detect malicious apps and other threats on the device
questions.e: Mobile endpoint security scans apps and links and can report threats to the MDM.

questions.q: What is a weakness of a pattern screen lock?
o: Smudge marks or someone watching can reveal the pattern
It only works with a fingerprint
questions.e: Patterns are easy to observe or work out from finger marks. A strong PIN or biometric is better.

questions.q: What would a configuration profile for corporate Wi-Fi on company phones typically include?
o: The network name, security type and the certificate or credentials to connect
A list of games to install
questions.e: Profiles pushed through MDM set up Wi-Fi, VPN, email and passcode rules automatically.

questions.q: Why doesn't degaussing work on SSDs?
o: SSDs store data electrically in flash memory, not magnetically
Degaussing only works on optical discs
questions.e: Degaussing disrupts magnetic fields, so it only works on magnetic media like HDDs and tapes.
questions.l: Extra practice: Data destruction and disposal

questions.q: Which physical destruction method cuts drives into small pieces?
questions.e: Industrial shredders reduce drives to small fragments so no data can be recovered.
questions.l: Extra practice: Data destruction and disposal

questions.q: A small office needs to destroy a few old hard drives on site with basic tools. Which is a reasonable method?
o: Putting them in the recycling bin
questions.e: Drilling physically damages the platters. For high-security data, use certified shredding.
questions.l: Extra practice: Data destruction and disposal

questions.q: Which destruction method burns drives completely?
questions.e: Incineration destroys media by burning it at very high temperatures, usually through a specialist firm.
questions.l: Extra practice: Data destruction and disposal

questions.q: What is the difference between a standard format and a low-level format or wipe?
o: A standard format mainly removes the file system index, while a wipe overwrites every sector
A standard format physically destroys the drive
A wipe only removes the recycle bin
questions.e: After a standard (quick) format, data can often be recovered. Overwriting the whole drive makes recovery very difficult.
questions.l: Extra practice: Data destruction and disposal

questions.q: What is the best way to securely erase an SSD so it can be reused?
o: Use the manufacturer's secure erase tool or the drive's built-in secure erase
questions.e: SSD secure erase resets every flash cell, including areas a normal overwrite can't reach.
questions.l: Extra practice: Data destruction and disposal

questions.q: Why do environmental rules matter when disposing of old drives and PCs?
o: E-waste contains hazardous materials and must go through approved recycling, such as under UK WEEE rules
They don't apply to IT equipment
They require drives to go in general waste
questions.e: Electronics contain metals and chemicals that harm the environment, so they must be recycled properly.
questions.l: Extra practice: Data destruction and disposal

questions.q: A company wants to donate old PCs to a local charity. What must happen first?
o: Securely wipe the drives so no company data can be recovered
questions.e: Repurposed drives must be wiped, not just formatted, before leaving the company.
questions.l: Extra practice: Data destruction and disposal

questions.q: Why keep a SOHO router's firmware up to date?
o: Updates fix security holes that attackers could use
questions.e: Router firmware often has vulnerabilities. Check for updates regularly or enable automatic updates.

questions.q: Why place a wireless router centrally and out of reach, rather than on a windowsill by the door?
o: It improves indoor coverage, limits signal leaking outside and stops people tampering with it
questions.e: Physical placement affects both coverage and security.

questions.q: What does content filtering on a SOHO router do?
o: Blocks access to websites or categories of content
questions.e: Content filtering can block categories like adult or gambling sites, or specific domains.

questions.q: What does IP filtering on a router do?
o: Allows or blocks traffic from specific IP addresses
questions.e: IP filtering is a simple allow or deny list based on addresses.

questions.q: Why give a network printer a DHCP reservation?
o: So it always gets the same IP address and users can keep finding it
So it can print in colour
So it doesn't need a driver
questions.e: A reservation ties an IP to the printer's MAC address while still using DHCP.

questions.q: Which firewall practice reduces risk on a SOHO router?
o: Close any ports that aren't needed
Forward every port to one PC
Turn the firewall off at night
questions.e: Only open ports that are needed, and forward them only to the device that needs them.

questions.q: Why should web browsers be kept updated?
o: Updates patch security vulnerabilities attackers could exploit
questions.e: Browsers are a common attack target, so patches matter. Most update automatically when restarted.

questions.q: What does the padlock in a browser's address bar tell you?
o: The connection is encrypted with a valid certificate, though it doesn't prove the site is honest
questions.e: Phishing sites can have valid certificates too. Always check the address as well.

questions.q: What is a security benefit of using a password manager?
o: It creates and stores strong, unique passwords and only fills them on the correct site
It shares passwords with colleagues automatically
It removes the need for MFA
questions.e: Because it matches the real site address, a password manager won't autofill on a lookalike phishing site.

questions.q: What does a browser's pop-up blocker protect against?
o: Unwanted windows that can contain adverts, scams or malicious links
questions.e: Pop-up blockers stop sites opening new windows without the user asking.

questions.q: A website keeps showing old content and won't log in properly. What should you clear first?
o: The browser cache and cookies for that site
questions.e: Old cached files and cookies can cause display and login problems.

questions.q: A user signs in to their browser on a shared library PC. What is the risk?
o: Their synced bookmarks, history and saved passwords could be available to the next person if they don't sign out
questions.e: Browser sync is useful on your own devices, but always sign out on shared ones.

questions.q: How does an ad blocker improve security?
o: It blocks adverts that might carry malicious code (malvertising)
It makes all sites use HTTPS
questions.e: Malicious ads can appear even on trusted sites. Ad blockers reduce that exposure.

questions.q: A company requires all web traffic to go through its filtering server. Where is this configured for the browser?
o: In the proxy settings (in Windows or the browser)
questions.e: The proxy server address and port can be set manually, by script or pushed with Group Policy.

questions.q: Windows warns about 'not enough USB controller resources' when lots of devices are plugged into a dock. What should you try?
o: Move some devices to ports on a different USB controller, such as directly on the PC
questions.e: Each USB controller has limited resources. Spreading devices across controllers or using fewer devices fixes it.

questions.q: One application crashes repeatedly, while everything else on the PC works fine. What should you try first?
o: Update, repair or reinstall that application
questions.e: When only one app is affected, start with that app before looking at Windows as a whole.

questions.q: A PC shuts down frequently without warning. Where should you look for clues?
o: Event Viewer, plus temperatures and power settings
questions.e: Event Viewer records unexpected shutdowns. Overheating and power problems are common causes.

questions.q: A PC has become slow over months, and many programs start at sign-in. What is a good first fix?
o: Disable unneeded startup apps in Task Manager
questions.e: Reducing startup programs frees up memory and speeds up sign-in.

questions.q: An app won't update from the app store. Which checks fit this?
o: Free storage space, the internet connection, and whether the app still supports the device
questions.e: Updates need storage, a working connection and a compatible OS version.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: A phone's battery drains much faster since a new app was installed. What should you check?
o: Battery usage in settings, then restrict or uninstall the app
Turn off the phone's lock screen
questions.e: Battery settings show which apps use the most power, including in the background.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: A phone has become slow to respond. Which is a sensible first step?
o: Close unused apps, restart the phone and free up storage
questions.e: A restart clears memory, and low storage can slow a phone down a lot.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: A phone won't connect to the office Wi-Fi, though colleagues' phones do. What should you try?
o: Forget the network and reconnect with the correct password
questions.e: Forgetting the network clears saved settings that may be wrong or out of date.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: An older phone can't install the latest OS update, even with plenty of storage. What is the likely reason?
o: The device is no longer supported by the manufacturer for that update
questions.e: Manufacturers stop updates for older models. Unsupported devices become a security risk over time.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: What is sideloading on a mobile device?
o: Installing apps from outside the official app store, such as an APK file
questions.e: Sideloaded apps skip the store's security checks, so they're a common route for malware.

questions.q: A user's private photos have appeared online. They recently installed a 'free' torch app that asked for access to everything. What is likely?
o: A malicious app has leaked their data, so remove it, review app permissions and change passwords
The cloud provider deleted the photos
questions.e: Leaked personal files are a sign of a malicious app. Remove it, check permissions and secure the accounts.

questions.q: A phone gets hot and sluggish while idle after a game was installed from an unofficial website. What is a likely cause?
o: Malware, such as a hidden cryptominer, running in the background
questions.e: Unexpected heat, slowness and battery drain while idle point to malicious background activity.

questions.q: Malware on a phone can't be removed by uninstalling apps. What is the safest fix?
o: Back up personal data, factory reset the phone and reinstall apps only from the official store
Root the phone to remove it
questions.e: A factory reset removes the malware. Don't restore apps from the same untrusted source.

questions.q: A user's files have been renamed or gone missing, and they didn't do it. What should you suspect?
o: Malware, so follow the malware removal process
questions.e: Altered, missing or inaccessible files are a classic malware symptom.

questions.q: Notifications from a website keep appearing on a user's Windows desktop even when the browser is closed. What is the fix?
o: Remove that site's notification permission in the browser settings
questions.e: Users are often tricked into clicking 'Allow' on notifications. Remove the permission in the browser's site settings.

questions.q: A browser has become very slow and has new toolbars the user didn't add. What should you do?
o: Remove the unwanted extensions or programs and reset the browser settings
questions.e: Unwanted toolbars and slowness point to adware or PUPs.

questions.q: A PC can't access the network, while others can, and its antivirus has switched itself off. What should you do?
o: Treat it as a likely infection: quarantine it and start malware removal
Turn the antivirus back on and carry on
questions.e: Malware often disables security tools and can interfere with networking.

questions.q: Pop-up adverts appear constantly, even on trusted websites. What is the likely cause?
o: Adware on the PC or in the browser
questions.e: Frequent pop-ups across all sites usually mean adware. Scan the PC and check extensions.

questions.q: Why shouldn't a user log in to online banking from a PC showing signs of malware?
o: A keylogger or other malware could capture their login details
The bank website will be slower
The PC will run out of storage
questions.e: Assume an infected PC can see everything typed on it until it's cleaned.

questions.q: A 'system cleaner' program the user never installed keeps showing alerts. What is it most likely to be?
o: A potentially unwanted program (PUP), which should be uninstalled
questions.e: PUPs are often bundled with other downloads. Remove them and check for anything else that came with them.

questions.q: What information goes on a change request form?
o: The purpose, scope, date and time, affected systems and risk level of the change
questions.e: A full request lets the CAB judge whether the change should go ahead.

questions.q: What is a 'normal' change in change management?
o: A change that needs full review and approval by the change advisory board
An urgent change during an outage
A change made without any record
questions.e: Standard changes are pre-approved, emergency changes are urgent, and normal changes go through the full process.

questions.q: Why carry out a risk analysis before a change?
o: To judge how likely problems are and how much impact they would have
To pick the colour of the new software
questions.e: The risk level helps decide approvals, timing and how detailed the rollback plan needs to be.

questions.q: What is peer review in change management?
o: Another technician checking the change plan or work before it goes ahead
Users testing the change after release
questions.e: A second pair of eyes catches mistakes before they reach live systems.

questions.q: Why should every change have a named responsible staff member?
o: So one person is accountable for carrying it out and dealing with problems
So everyone can blame each other
questions.e: Clear ownership means someone is responsible from planning to sign-off.

questions.q: A user restores an old version of a file into a different folder, so the current version isn't overwritten. What is this called?
questions.e: Restoring to an alternative location lets you compare versions before replacing anything.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of keeping one backup copy offsite?
o: It survives a fire, flood or theft at the main site
It restores faster than onsite backups
questions.e: Onsite copies are quick to restore. Offsite copies protect against disasters that hit the whole building.

questions.q: A full backup runs Sunday with incrementals Monday to Thursday. The drive fails on Friday morning. What is needed to restore everything?
o: Sunday's full backup plus every incremental from Monday to Thursday
Sunday's full and Thursday's incremental only
questions.e: Each incremental only holds changes since the previous backup, so all of them are needed in order.

questions.q: Which type of backup is the quickest to restore from?
questions.e: A full backup has everything in one set. Incrementals restore slowest because each one is needed in turn.

questions.q: What is an in-place restore?
o: Restoring data back to its original location, overwriting what's there
Testing a backup without restoring it
questions.e: In-place (overwrite) restores replace the current files with the backup copies.

questions.q: Why use an ESD mat as well as a wrist strap?
o: The mat grounds the components you put down on it
It replaces the need for a strap
questions.e: The strap grounds you and the mat grounds the parts, so there's no charge difference between them.

questions.q: A technician has to run a network cable across a busy walkway. What should they do?
o: Route it safely or cover it to prevent a trip hazard
Leave it loose and warn people
Run it through a doorway so the door closes on it
questions.e: Cable management keeps cables tidy and out of the way to prevent trips and damage.

questions.q: Which personal protective equipment should you wear when blowing dust out of a very dusty PC?
o: Safety goggles and a dust mask
questions.e: Compressed air throws dust into the air and towards your eyes.

questions.q: Why is equipment grounding important?
o: It gives fault current a safe path, protecting people from electric shock
questions.e: Proper earthing means a fault trips the circuit instead of making the case live.

questions.q: Which rules must a technician follow when doing physical work on site in the UK?
o: Health and safety regulations and the employer's safety policies
None, if the work is quick
questions.e: Compliance with government regulations is part of CompTIA's safety objective. In the UK that includes HSE rules.

questions.q: Why should you never open a power supply unit, even when it's unplugged?
o: Its capacitors can hold a dangerous charge long after power is removed
questions.e: PSUs are field-replaceable units. Replace them whole, don't repair them.

questions.q: What is a blackout?
o: A complete loss of mains power
questions.e: A brownout is a voltage drop, a surge or spike is a sudden increase, and a blackout is total loss.

questions.q: Why is very low humidity a problem in a server room?
o: It increases the risk of static electricity damaging components
questions.e: Dry air makes ESD more likely. High humidity brings the opposite risk: condensation and corrosion.

questions.q: Why shouldn't a desktop PC be kept running inside a closed cupboard?
o: Poor ventilation can make it overheat
questions.e: Equipment needs airflow to remove heat. Keep vents clear and dust down.

questions.q: How should used toner cartridges be disposed of?
o: Recycle them through the manufacturer or an approved scheme, following the SDS
Empty the toner into a sink
questions.e: Toner is a fine powder that can harm people and the environment, so it needs proper recycling.

questions.q: What is the difference between a surge protector and a UPS?
o: A surge protector only guards against spikes, while a UPS also gives battery power during a cut
They do exactly the same thing
A UPS only protects against spikes
A surge protector has a battery
questions.e: Surge protectors don't keep anything running in a power cut. A UPS gives time to shut down safely.

questions.q: While fixing a PC you find what looks like illegal content. What should you do first?
o: Stop, don't investigate further, and report it to management following company policy
Copy it to a USB stick to show colleagues
Ignore it and finish the job
questions.e: Preserve the evidence and follow the incident response policy. Deleting or copying it could destroy evidence or break the law.
questions.l: Extra practice: Privacy, licensing and policy

questions.q: What is the difference between a personal and a corporate software licence?
o: A personal licence is for home use, while businesses need commercial or corporate licences
Personal licences can be used on unlimited PCs
questions.e: Using personal licences for business work usually breaks the licence terms.
questions.l: Extra practice: Privacy, licensing and policy

questions.q: What does an open-source licence usually allow?
o: Viewing, changing and sharing the source code, within the licence's terms
Using the software with no rules at all
Selling it as your own closed product with no conditions
Nothing, it's the same as proprietary software
questions.e: Open source is still licensed. Licences like GPL and MIT each set their own conditions.
questions.l: Extra practice: Privacy, licensing and policy

questions.q: What are data retention requirements?
o: Rules on how long certain data must be kept, and when it should be deleted
Rules on how fast data can be downloaded
questions.e: Laws and company policy may require keeping records, such as financial ones, for set periods.
questions.l: Extra practice: Privacy, licensing and policy

questions.q: Your personal phone keeps buzzing while you're helping a customer. What should you do?
o: Ignore it or silence it, and only answer if it's a genuine emergency
Answer it in front of the customer
questions.e: Avoid distractions like personal calls, texts and social media while working with customers.

questions.q: A customer is explaining their problem in a lot of detail. What should you do?
o: Listen actively, take notes and don't interrupt
Cut them off and start fixing
Finish their sentences to save time
questions.e: Active listening helps you get the full picture and shows the customer respect.

questions.q: A repair is going to take longer than you promised. What should you do?
o: Tell the customer promptly and give a new timeline and options
Say nothing and hope they don't notice
Tell them it's done when it isn't
questions.e: Setting and meeting expectations includes keeping customers updated on progress.

questions.q: How should you address a customer you've just met?
o: Formally, using their title and surname, unless they tell you otherwise
By their first name only, always
questions.e: Using titles is culturally sensitive and professional. Follow the customer's lead.

questions.q: After a difficult call, a technician wants to post about the customer on social media. Is that acceptable?
o: No, never post about customers or their problems on social media
Yes, if they don't use the customer's name
questions.e: Discussing customers publicly is unprofessional and can breach confidentiality.

questions.q: Why give a customer the option to repair or replace a faulty device?
o: It lets them make an informed choice about cost and time
It makes the job take longer
questions.e: Offering options is part of setting expectations and good customer service.

questions.q: Which file extension is a JavaScript file?
questions.e: .js is JavaScript, .sh is a shell script, .py is Python and .bat is a Windows batch file.

questions.q: A script runs at sign-in to connect users to their shared folders as drive letters. Which use case is this?
questions.e: Logon scripts often map drives so users always see the same network locations.

questions.q: An admin writes a script to collect serial numbers and RAM sizes from every PC. Which use case is this?
questions.e: Scripts are handy for inventory and reporting across many machines.

questions.q: Why should a new script be tested in a sandbox or VM before running it on live PCs?
o: It could change system settings in ways you didn't intend
Scripts never work first time on real hardware
It makes the script run faster
It's needed to save the file
questions.e: Untested scripts can break settings, delete files or crash systems.

questions.q: Why should you only run scripts from trusted sources?
o: A script from an unknown source could introduce malware
Trusted scripts don't need admin rights
Unknown scripts only work on Linux
questions.e: Scripts run with the user's permissions (or more), so a malicious one can do real damage.

questions.q: A scheduled script reboots all the kiosk PCs at 3am every night. Which use case is this?
questions.e: Scheduled restarts clear memory and apply pending updates outside opening hours.

questions.q: A script silently installs a new app on 50 PCs. Which use case is this?
questions.e: Scripts can install software consistently across many machines without anyone clicking through setup.

questions.q: What does a VPN provide for staff working from home?
o: An encrypted tunnel to the company network over the internet
questions.e: A VPN protects traffic between the remote user and the office network.

questions.q: A help desk technician uses screen-sharing software to fix a user's PC. What is good practice?
o: Get the user's permission, let them watch, and end the session when finished
questions.e: Users should know when someone is connected. Unattended open sessions are a security risk.

questions.q: Which security setting helps stop uninvited people joining a video call?
o: A meeting password or waiting room so the host admits attendees
Sharing the link on social media
questions.e: Video conferencing tools used for support should be locked down to invited participants.

questions.q: Which type of tool lets admins manage company PCs centrally, pushing software, updates and policies (for example, Microsoft Intune)?
questions.e: Desktop management tools handle deployment, configuration and reporting for many devices.

questions.q: Which remote access method gives secure command-line access to a Linux server?
questions.e: SSH encrypts the whole session on port 22. Telnet sends everything, including passwords, in plain text.

questions.q: Why shouldn't staff paste customer data into a public AI chatbot?
o: The data could be stored or used by the provider, breaching privacy rules like GDPR
questions.e: Public AI tools may keep prompts. Company policy should say what data can and can't be entered.

questions.q: An AI tool suggests a PowerShell script to fix a problem. What should the technician do?
o: Read it, understand it and test it safely before running it on live systems
Run it straight away as admin
Assume it's correct because AI wrote it
questions.e: AI output can be wrong or harmful, so it should be checked like any untrusted script.

questions.q: What is meant by AI application integration?
o: AI features built into existing apps, such as an assistant inside an office suite
Installing AI on a separate server only
questions.e: Many tools now include AI features. Admins need to decide how they're configured and what data they can reach.

questions.q: Why might an AI tool give out-of-date answers?
o: It was trained on data up to a certain point and may not know about newer changes
It's always connected to live data
It only uses the user's files
questions.e: Check AI answers about recent software versions, prices or policies against current sources.

questions.q: What should a company's appropriate use policy for AI cover?
o: Which AI tools are allowed, what data can be entered and how output must be checked
Only the colour scheme of the AI tool
Nothing, AI doesn't need a policy
questions.e: Clear rules reduce data leaks, plagiarism and mistakes from unchecked AI output.

questions.q: Why does it matter what data an AI model was trained on?
o: The data source affects its accuracy and any bias in its answers
It only affects how fast it responds
questions.e: Poor or unbalanced training data leads to inaccurate or biased results.

questions.q: How can a support team reduce the risk of AI hallucinations in answers they give customers?
o: Check the AI's answers against official documentation before using them
Ask the AI the same question twice
questions.e: AI can sound confident while being wrong. A human check against trusted sources catches errors.

questions.q: Which is a sensible use of AI in an IT support team?
o: Drafting knowledge base articles or summarising tickets, with a person reviewing the result
Approving changes instead of the CAB
Making final decisions about user access with no checks
questions.e: AI works well as an assistant. A person should still review anything that goes to users or affects systems.

questions.q: What is a Type 2 hypervisor?
o: One that runs as an application on top of a normal operating system
One that runs directly on the hardware with no host OS
A hypervisor that only runs containers
A cloud service for storing VMs
questions.e: Type 2 examples are VirtualBox and VMware Workstation. Type 1 (bare-metal) examples are ESXi and Hyper-V.

questions.q: Which of these is a Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor?
questions.e: ESXi installs directly on the server hardware. The others run as apps inside an existing OS.

questions.q: Before installing a risky update inside a VM, what can you take so you can roll back if it goes wrong?
questions.e: Snapshots save a VM's state at a point in time. Hyper-V calls them checkpoints.

questions.q: A Mac user needs to run a Windows-only accounting app. Which is a common solution?
o: Run Windows in a virtual machine on the Mac
Install the app on the Mac's router
Format the Mac's drive as NTFS
questions.e: Cross-platform virtualisation lets one OS run another's apps, for example with Parallels or VMware Fusion.

questions.q: Developers need to test an app on Windows 10, Windows 11 and Ubuntu without buying extra PCs. What is the best approach?
o: Run each OS in its own virtual machine
Install all three on one partition
Use a single container for all three
questions.e: Test and development is one of the main reasons for virtualisation. VMs can be created, reset and deleted quickly.

questions.q: A host PC has 16 GB of RAM. A user tries to run three VMs at once, each given 8 GB. What is the likely result?
o: The host runs out of memory, so performance suffers or a VM won't start
The VMs share 24 GB without any issue
The hypervisor adds RAM from the cloud
questions.e: The host needs enough RAM for itself plus every running VM. Plan CPU, RAM and storage before creating VMs.

questions.q: What is a 'VM escape'?
o: An attack where malware breaks out of a VM to reach the host or other VMs
Moving a VM to another host
A VM losing its network connection
questions.e: VM escape is the key reason to keep hypervisors patched. If the host is compromised, every VM on it is at risk.

questions.q: An analyst wants a malware test VM that can't reach the company network. Which VM network setting fits best?
o: Connecting it to the office Wi-Fi
Giving it a public IP address
questions.e: Isolated virtual networks keep a test VM away from real systems.

questions.q: Which VM network mode gives the VM its own IP address on the physical network, as if it were a separate PC?
questions.e: Bridged connects the VM straight to the real network. NAT shares the host's address, and host-only or internal networks stay private.

questions.q: Why does a virtualisation host need plenty of fast storage?
o: Each VM's virtual disk is a large file, and several VMs reading and writing at once need good performance
Fast storage replaces the need for RAM
questions.e: Virtual disks (such as .vhdx or .vmdk files) can be tens of gigabytes each, and slow drives make every VM slow.

questions.q: Which is a widely used platform for building and running containers?
questions.e: Docker packages an app with its dependencies into a container. Kubernetes is often used to manage many containers.

questions.q: A company has hundreds of remote staff. What is a benefit of giving them virtual desktops (VDI) instead of full laptops?
o: Desktops and data are managed centrally in the data centre, so little is stored on the user's device
Users never need an internet connection
It removes the need for any servers
questions.e: With VDI, the desktop runs on central servers and the user's device just displays it, which simplifies management and security.

questions.q: Why must the virtualisation host itself be well secured?
o: If an attacker controls the host, they can reach every VM running on it
The host never connects to a network
questions.e: Keep the host patched, limit admin access and separate management traffic, because the host is a single point of failure.

questions.q: What is a private cloud?
o: Cloud infrastructure used by one organisation only, either on its own premises or hosted for it
A cloud anyone can sign up to
A cloud shared by organisations in the same industry
Cloud storage on a USB stick
questions.e: Private cloud gives more control and isolation, but the organisation pays for and manages more of it.

questions.q: A company rents virtual servers through IaaS. Who is responsible for patching the operating system on those servers?
o: Nobody, as cloud servers don't need patches
questions.e: With IaaS the provider runs the hardware, but the customer manages the OS and everything installed on it.

questions.q: With a SaaS product like Microsoft 365, who maintains and updates the application itself?
questions.e: In SaaS the provider manages everything up to the app. The customer manages users, settings and their own data.

questions.q: What is a financial benefit of moving to the cloud instead of buying servers?
o: You pay for what you use, without a large upfront hardware cost
You never need an internet connection
questions.e: Cloud turns big one-off hardware purchases into ongoing operating costs that can scale up or down.

questions.q: In cloud billing, what is ingress?
o: Data going into the cloud provider, which is usually free
Data leaving the provider, which is usually charged
The cost of extra virtual CPUs
questions.e: Ingress is data in, egress is data out. Providers usually charge for egress, not ingress.

questions.q: Why might a company run its cloud service across several regions or availability zones?
o: So the service keeps running if one data centre has an outage
questions.e: Spreading resources across locations is a key way to get high availability.

questions.q: A company adds more cloud servers over several years as it slowly grows. Which term best describes this?
questions.e: Scalability is growing capacity to meet long-term demand. Elasticity is automatic scaling up and down in response to short-term spikes.

questions.q: Which is a drawback of relying on public cloud services?
o: Everything depends on a working internet connection, and you have less control over the hardware
You must buy all the servers yourself
Data can never be backed up
questions.e: If the internet link goes down, cloud apps become unavailable. Many businesses have a backup connection for this reason.

questions.q: UK regulations say a company's customer data must stay in the UK. What should they check with a cloud provider?
o: Which region or country the data will be stored in
How many staff the provider has
The colour of the provider's logo
questions.e: Most providers let you choose a region. Data residency rules affect where data can legally be stored.

questions.q: An online shop's traffic drops after the January sales. How does rapid elasticity help?
o: Resources scale back down automatically, so they stop paying for capacity they don't need
It makes the website go offline
It increases the price per user
It moves the data onto staff laptops
questions.e: Elasticity works both ways: scaling up for peaks and back down when demand falls.

questions.q: Who owns and maintains the physical hardware in a public cloud?
questions.e: Customers rent capacity on the provider's servers, storage and networks.
