questions.q: A company runs most systems in its private cloud but uses public cloud when it runs out of capacity at busy times. What is this called?
o: Cloud bursting, a common use of hybrid cloud
questions.e: Hybrid cloud lets workloads overflow into public cloud when private resources are full.

questions.q: What should a business check in a cloud provider's service-level agreement (SLA)?
o: The guaranteed uptime, support response times and what happens if they miss them
The provider's office opening hours only
How many customers the provider has
questions.e: The SLA sets out what the provider commits to, such as 99.9% availability, and any compensation for missing it.

questions.q: You're taking a laptop apart to replace a part. What helps most with putting it back together correctly?
o: Labelling or photographing screws and cables and keeping them organised as you go
Putting all the screws in one pile
Removing every part even if it isn't needed
Working without the lights on to avoid glare
questions.e: Screws are often different lengths. Documenting and labelling where everything came from avoids damage on reassembly.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile hardware and replacement

questions.q: What should you check before opening a laptop you haven't worked on before?
o: The manufacturer's service manual or support resources for that model
questions.e: Service manuals show the right order of steps, hidden screws and clips, and part numbers.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile hardware and replacement

questions.q: Several keys on a laptop stopped working after a coffee spill. What is the usual fix?
questions.e: Laptop keyboards are usually replaced as a whole unit. On some models the keyboard is part of the top case.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile hardware and replacement

questions.q: Why do many laptops have a sliding cover over the webcam?
o: It's a physical privacy shutter, so the camera can't see anything even if it's turned on
It makes the camera work in the dark
questions.e: Privacy shutters and microphone mute switches are physical privacy controls on mobile devices.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile hardware and replacement

questions.q: How can you check a Windows laptop's battery health?
o: Run powercfg /batteryreport and compare the full charge capacity with the design capacity
questions.e: The battery report shows how much charge the battery can hold now compared with when it was new.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile hardware and replacement

questions.q: A user's laptop HDD is being replaced with an SSD. How can they keep their OS, apps and files?
o: Clone the old drive to the new SSD with cloning software
Install the SSD without the OS
questions.e: Cloning copies the whole drive, including the OS and boot data, so the laptop boots from the SSD as before.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile hardware and replacement

questions.q: A user wants more RAM in their thin laptop. What should you check first?
o: Whether the RAM is soldered to the board or in SO-DIMM slots, plus the type and maximum supported
Whether the laptop has a webcam
questions.e: Many thin laptops have soldered RAM that can't be upgraded. Check the specs before buying.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile hardware and replacement

questions.q: Which precaution should you take before working inside a laptop?
o: Power it off, unplug the charger and use ESD protection
Leave it on so you can test as you go
questions.e: Static can damage laptop components just as easily as desktop ones.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile hardware and replacement

questions.q: You've replaced a laptop's Wi-Fi card. What must be reconnected to the new card?
questions.e: Wi-Fi cards have small antenna connectors, often marked main and aux. Without them the signal will be very weak.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile hardware and replacement

questions.q: Besides the screen, which parts are often found in a laptop's lid?
o: The webcam, microphone and Wi-Fi antennas
questions.e: Remember the lid components when replacing a screen, as their cables run through the hinge.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile hardware and replacement

questions.q: Why should a replacement laptop battery be a manufacturer-approved part?
o: Cheap or incompatible batteries can overheat, swell or fail to charge properly
Unapproved batteries make the screen brighter
questions.e: Lithium batteries need the right protection circuits. A poor-quality battery is a safety risk.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile hardware and replacement

questions.q: A modern laptop's battery is built in rather than removable. What does replacing it involve?
o: Opening the case following the service manual and unplugging the battery connector before removing it
Pulling it out through the charging port
questions.e: Internal batteries are often held by screws or adhesive. Follow the manual and handle them carefully.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile hardware and replacement

questions.q: Why should you disconnect a laptop's internal battery before replacing other internal parts?
o: To avoid short circuits and damage while you work
questions.e: Even with the laptop off, the battery still supplies power to the board.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile hardware and replacement

questions.q: A single USB-C cable from a monitor charges a laptop and shows its picture. Which USB-C features make this possible?
o: USB Power Delivery and DisplayPort Alternate Mode
questions.e: USB-C can carry power, data and video at the same time when the port and device support it.

questions.q: Can every USB-C port output video to a monitor?
o: No, it depends on whether that port supports video, such as DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt
questions.e: USB-C is just the connector shape. Check the port's symbol or the device specs for video support.

questions.q: A laptop's built-in webcam has failed and the user has a video call today. What is the quickest fix?
o: Plug in an external USB webcam
questions.e: Most USB webcams are plug and play, so they work straight away without opening the laptop.

questions.q: When turning on a phone's personal hotspot, what should be set?
o: A strong password using WPA2 or WPA3
No password, so others can join easily
The phone's IMEI as the password
questions.e: An open hotspot lets anyone nearby use your data and potentially see your traffic.

questions.q: What is a downside of using a phone as a hotspot for a laptop?
o: It uses the phone's mobile data allowance and drains its battery
It makes the laptop's Wi-Fi card stop working
It only works with Bluetooth headsets
questions.e: Hotspots are handy, but large downloads can quickly use a data cap.

questions.q: What is the typical range of NFC?
questions.e: NFC's very short range is part of why it suits contactless payments and tap-to-pair.

questions.q: What does a port replicator do?
o: Gives a laptop extra ports through a single connection
questions.e: A port replicator duplicates ports like USB, video and Ethernet so you only plug in one cable at the desk.

questions.q: Why doesn't a basic passive (capacitive) stylus need pairing with a tablet?
o: It works like a fingertip on the touchscreen and has no electronics to connect
It connects through the charging port
questions.e: Active styluses have electronics for pressure and buttons and may need pairing or charging. Passive ones don't.

questions.q: A laptop only has USB-C ports, and the user needs to connect an HDMI projector and a USB-A memory stick. What do they need?
o: A USB-C hub or adapter with HDMI and USB-A ports
questions.e: USB-C hubs (often called dongles) add the older ports thin laptops leave out.

questions.q: A network engineer needs to connect a laptop to a switch's serial console port. Which accessory might they need?
questions.e: Many network devices still use serial (RS-232) console ports, while modern laptops don't have serial ports.

questions.q: Which connector is mostly found on older Android phones and small accessories?
questions.e: Micro-USB was the standard before USB-C. It's still common on cheap accessories.

questions.q: What is an advantage of USB tethering over a Wi-Fi hotspot?
o: The phone charges while sharing, and the wired link avoids Wi-Fi interference and can't be joined by nearby devices
It doesn't use any mobile data
questions.e: USB tethering avoids Wi-Fi interference and keeps the phone's battery topped up.

questions.q: A user takes calls in a noisy open-plan office. Which accessory helps others hear them clearly?
o: A headset with a noise-cancelling microphone
questions.e: Headsets with noise-cancelling mics cut out background sound on calls.

questions.q: What is the final step when pairing a Bluetooth device?
o: Test the connection to confirm it works
questions.e: The pairing steps are: enable Bluetooth, put the device in pairing mode, pair, enter or confirm the PIN, then test.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: When adding a work email account that uses MFA to a phone, what will the user usually also need?
o: Their authenticator app or another second factor to approve the sign-in
questions.e: The phone's mail app will hand off to the company's sign-in page, which asks for the second factor.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: A company wants staff to install work apps only from an approved list on their managed phones. Which tool provides this?
questions.e: MDM and MAM tools can push approved apps and block or remove others.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: An iPhone user buys a Mac and wants their photos and contacts to appear on it automatically. Which account handles this?
questions.e: iCloud syncs photos, contacts, calendars and more across the user's Apple devices.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: A work Android phone is set up with a Google Workspace account. What usually syncs?
o: Gmail, Calendar, Contacts and Drive files
questions.e: Google Workspace accounts sync email, calendar, contacts and cloud files, much like Microsoft 365.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: Indoors, where GPS signal is weak, how does a phone still work out its location?
o: Using nearby mobile phone masts and Wi-Fi networks
It can't find its location at all
questions.e: Location services combine GPS with cellular and Wi-Fi positioning.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: A user has weak mobile signal at home but good Wi-Fi. Which feature helps them make calls?
questions.e: Wi-Fi calling routes normal phone calls over the internet when mobile signal is poor.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: A user wants a video streaming app to work only on Wi-Fi so it can't use their mobile data. What should they do?
o: Turn off mobile data for that app in Settings
questions.e: iOS and Android both let you block mobile data per app while leaving it on for everything else.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: A laptop connects to a phone's hotspot but gets no internet. What should you check?
o: That mobile data is on and the phone's plan allows hotspot use
That the laptop's Bluetooth is off
questions.e: Some mobile plans block or limit tethering. The phone itself also needs a working data connection.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: An old Bluetooth speaker keeps connecting to a user's phone automatically. How do they stop it?
o: Forget (unpair) the device in the phone's Bluetooth settings
questions.e: Forgetting a device removes the pairing so it won't reconnect.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: A user is getting a new phone and uses an authenticator app for work sign-ins. What should they do before wiping the old phone?
o: Transfer or re-register the authenticator on the new phone
Nothing, as the codes move automatically
questions.e: If the old phone is wiped first, they can be locked out until IT resets their MFA.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: A phone shows 'This device is managed by your organisation'. Which is something IT can typically do through MDM?
o: Apply security policies, install work apps and wipe company data
Read the user's personal text messages
Change the user's mobile phone contract
Turn the phone into a desktop PC
questions.e: MDM controls settings and work data. On BYOD devices, work profiles keep personal data separate.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: Automatic setup fails when adding a corporate email account to a phone. What does manual setup usually ask for?
o: The email address, the mail server name, and the username and password
The phone's IMEI and battery level
questions.e: If autodiscovery fails, the mail app needs the server details from IT. Many companies push these through MDM instead.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile connectivity and app support

questions.q: Which simple step fixes a surprising number of Windows problems and should be tried early?
questions.e: A reboot clears memory, restarts services and finishes pending updates.

questions.q: Windows became unstable after a new app was installed, and uninstalling the app didn't help. Which tool can roll the system back?
o: System Restore, to a point before the install
questions.e: System Restore rolls back system files, drivers and settings without touching the user's documents.

questions.q: Windows won't boot after an update. Which environment offers Startup Repair, System Restore and uninstalling updates?
questions.e: WinRE opens automatically after repeated failed boots, or from installation media.

questions.q: When is reimaging a PC the right fix?
o: When other fixes have failed, after backing up the user's data
As the first step for any problem
Whenever the user forgets their password
questions.e: Reimaging is reliable but wipes the PC, so it's usually a last resort.

questions.q: Windows has many corrupted files that sfc can't fix, and the user wants to keep their apps and files. What should you try?
questions.e: A repair (in-place) install replaces Windows system files while keeping apps, settings and data.

questions.q: A new game crashes every time it starts on an older PC. What should you check first?
o: Whether the PC meets the game's minimum system requirements
questions.e: Games list minimum CPU, RAM and GPU requirements. Hardware below them, or an outdated GPU driver, often causes crashes.

questions.q: A PC shows a blue screen with a stop code. How can you find out more about the cause?
o: Note the stop code and check Event Viewer or the crash dump files
Ignore the code and reinstall Windows
questions.e: Stop codes and crash dumps often point to a specific driver or hardware fault.

questions.q: An app needs a Windows service that keeps not running after a restart. In services.msc, the service is set to Manual. What should you change?
o: Set its startup type to Automatic
questions.e: Automatic starts the service at boot. Automatic (Delayed Start) starts it shortly after boot.

questions.q: Windows still boots but has problems, and you want to open the Windows Recovery Environment. What is a quick way in?
questions.e: Shift + Restart opens the advanced startup options. You can also reach WinRE from Settings > System > Recovery.

questions.q: Before rebuilding a user's corrupted Windows profile, what must you do first?
o: Back up the user's data from the old profile
questions.e: The user's documents, desktop and settings live in the profile folder, so save them before removing it.

questions.q: A PC has random crashes since new RAM was installed. Which built-in tool should you run?
questions.e: Faulty or incompatible RAM causes instability. Windows Memory Diagnostic tests it on the next restart.

questions.q: sfc /scannow reports it found corrupt files but couldn't fix some of them. Which command can repair the files it needs?
questions.e: DISM repairs the Windows component store that sfc uses. Run sfc again afterwards.

questions.q: Windows is very slow and Task Manager shows the disk at 100% almost constantly. What should you do?
o: Find which process is using the disk, check the drive's health and consider an SSD upgrade
questions.e: Constant 100% disk use is common on old HDDs and can also be a failing drive or a runaway process.

questions.q: An Android app keeps crashing, but other apps are fine. What can you try before reinstalling it?
o: Clear the app's cache (and then its data if needed) in Settings
questions.e: Corrupt cached data often causes crashes. Clearing data resets the app as if it were new.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: An app has frozen and won't close normally. What should you do?
questions.e: Force closing ends the app completely so it can be reopened cleanly.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: A phone screen won't rotate in any app. What should you check first?
o: Whether rotation lock is turned on
questions.e: Rotation lock is a quick toggle in the control centre or quick settings and is easy to turn on by accident.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: A user wants their phone battery to last longer through the day. Which change helps?
o: Lower the screen brightness and limit background app activity, or use low power mode
Turn on every radio at once
Increase the screen timeout to never
questions.e: The screen and background activity are the biggest battery drains.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: A phone has started rebooting randomly. Which checks fit this symptom?
o: Install OS updates, remove recently added apps and check the battery isn't overheating or failing
questions.e: Random reboots can come from buggy apps, OS bugs or a failing battery. A factory reset is the last resort.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: A phone connects to hotel Wi-Fi but can't load any websites. What is a likely reason?
o: The network has a sign-in (captive portal) page that hasn't been completed
questions.e: Many public networks need you to accept terms or log in on a web page before the internet works.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: After a user gets a new phone, it won't connect to their car's Bluetooth. What should you try?
o: Remove the old pairing on both the car and phone, then pair again
questions.e: Old or corrupt pairings stop a new connection. Clearing both sides and re-pairing usually fixes it.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: An app won't install and the phone says 'insufficient storage'. What should you do?
o: Free up space by removing unused apps, old media or cached data
questions.e: Phones need free space to download and unpack apps and updates.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: Before factory resetting a user's phone, what must you do?
o: Back up their data and make sure they know their account login
questions.e: After a reset, the phone may ask for the previous account (factory reset protection) before it can be used.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: An Android phone is behaving badly, and you suspect a third-party app. Which mode helps confirm this?
o: Safe mode, which starts the phone with only built-in apps
questions.e: If the problem goes away in safe mode, a downloaded app is the likely cause.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: An OS update won't start, and the phone shows the battery at 15%. What should you do?
o: Charge it or plug it in, then retry the update
questions.e: Phones block updates on low battery so they don't switch off part-way through.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: An app store says an app is 'not compatible with your device'. What is the likely reason?
o: The phone's OS version or hardware doesn't meet the app's requirements
The phone's ringtone is too loud
The user has too many contacts
questions.e: Apps set a minimum OS version and sometimes need specific hardware.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: An iPhone app has started crashing since the latest iOS update. What should you try?
o: Update the app, or delete and reinstall it
questions.e: Developers release app updates to fix problems with new OS versions.
questions.l: Extra practice: Mobile OS and app troubleshooting

questions.q: An app on a user's phone starts sending text messages by itself. What does this suggest?
o: The app is malicious and should be removed
questions.e: Unexpected app behaviour, especially messages or calls the user didn't make, is a sign of malware.

questions.q: How can a user check an app is genuine before installing it from the store?
o: Check the developer name, reviews and download numbers
Install it and see what happens
questions.e: App spoofing uses copycat names and icons. The developer name is the best giveaway.

questions.q: Which Android setting lets an app install other apps from APK files?
o: 'Install unknown apps', which should normally be left off
questions.e: Android grants unknown-source installs per app, such as allowing a browser or file manager to install APKs.

questions.q: Why might a company's MDM block a jailbroken iPhone from accessing work data?
o: Jailbreaking bypasses the built-in security controls, so the device can't be trusted
questions.e: MDM compliance checks often detect jailbreaks or rooting and block access until the device is restored.

questions.q: A phone has a VPN or configuration profile installed that the user doesn't recognise, and some sites won't load. What should you suspect?
o: A malicious profile intercepting the phone's traffic, which should be removed
questions.e: Rogue profiles and VPNs can redirect traffic through an attacker. Check them in Settings.

questions.q: A user suspects an app is causing high network traffic. Where can they confirm this?
o: The phone's data usage settings, which show data used per app
questions.e: Data usage per app quickly shows anything sending or receiving far more than expected.

questions.q: A user's personal data has been leaked through a malicious app. After removing the app, what else should they do?
o: Change their passwords and turn on MFA for important accounts
questions.e: Assume any credentials on the phone were exposed and secure those accounts.

questions.q: A phone's mobile data usage spikes overnight while the user is asleep and not using it. What is a likely cause?
o: An app, possibly malicious, running in the background
questions.e: Unexplained background data is a classic sign of malware or a misbehaving app.

questions.q: A suspicious Android app can't be uninstalled because it has device administrator rights. What should you do?
o: Remove its device admin permission in Settings (or use safe mode), then uninstall it
questions.e: Malware often grabs admin rights to protect itself. Removing that permission lets you uninstall it.

questions.q: Which permissions should worry you for a simple calculator app?
o: Access to SMS messages, contacts and the microphone
questions.e: A calculator doesn't need any of those. Over-reaching permissions are a red flag.

questions.q: Apps the user never installed have appeared on their phone. What should you do?
o: Treat it as a possible compromise: remove them, scan the phone and reset it if they come back
questions.e: Unknown apps appearing can mean malware or someone else having access to the device.

questions.q: A banking app refuses to run on a user's Android phone and says the device is rooted. What is the fix?
o: Restore the phone to its official, unrooted firmware
Install the app from an APK site
questions.e: Banking apps check for rooting because it weakens the phone's security.

questions.q: What does Google Play Protect do?
o: Scans apps on Android devices for harmful behaviour
questions.e: Play Protect checks apps from the Play Store and elsewhere and can warn about or remove harmful ones.

questions.q: Which Windows file can malware edit to redirect websites to the wrong IP address?
questions.e: The hosts file maps names to IPs before DNS is used, so malware edits it to redirect sites.

questions.q: A PC suddenly can't reach any websites, and you find a proxy server set in Windows that nobody configured. What is likely?
o: Malware changed the proxy settings to intercept or block traffic
questions.e: Unexpected proxy or DNS settings are common malware changes. Reset them and scan the PC.

questions.q: A PC's DNS settings point to an unknown server, and some websites look slightly wrong. What could this cause?
o: Redirection to fake sites that look like the real ones
questions.e: Rogue DNS servers can send users to phishing copies of real sites.

questions.q: Every HTTPS website shows a certificate warning, even well-known ones. What should you check first?
o: The PC's date and time, then look for malware or rogue certificates
questions.e: A wrong clock makes valid certificates look expired. If the clock is right, something may be intercepting traffic.

questions.q: A full-screen 'Windows Defender' alert tells the user to call a support number to remove a virus. What is it?
o: A tech support scam, as Microsoft never asks you to call a number from a pop-up
questions.e: Genuine Microsoft security alerts never include a phone number. Close the browser (with Task Manager if needed) and never call or allow remote access.

questions.q: After malware is removed, Windows still behaves oddly and some system files seem changed. What should you run?
questions.e: Malware can modify system files. sfc checks and replaces them with good copies.

questions.q: A browser is very slow and Task Manager shows it using high CPU on one website. What could be the cause?
o: A cryptojacking script on that site using the PC to mine cryptocurrency
questions.e: Some malicious sites run mining scripts in the browser. Closing the tab stops it; blockers can prevent it.

questions.q: Windows updates keep failing, and you find malware on the PC. What order should you work in?
o: Remove the malware first, then install the updates
Install updates first and leave the malware
questions.e: Malware often blocks updates. Clean the PC, then patch it so it isn't reinfected the same way.

questions.q: A user notices Windows Firewall has been turned off, and they didn't do it. What should you suspect?
questions.e: Turning off security tools is a common malware tactic. Turn it back on and scan the PC.

questions.q: A PC has been hit by ransomware. What should you do?
o: Isolate it from the network and restore files from a clean backup rather than paying
Email the ransom note to all staff
questions.e: Paying doesn't guarantee the files back. Isolate, report it and recover from backups.

questions.q: A user's contacts are getting spam emails sent from the user's real account. What should you do?
o: Treat the account as compromised: change the password, turn on MFA and check for unknown mail rules
Tell the user to ignore it
questions.e: Attackers often add forwarding or delete rules to hide what they're doing.

questions.q: A browser's homepage keeps changing back to an unknown site even after you reset the browser. What should you do?
o: Run a full malware scan, as something on the PC keeps reapplying the change
questions.e: PUPs and malware can use scheduled tasks or services to reapply browser changes.

questions.q: Antivirus quarantines a file the user says is a work tool they need. What should you do?
o: Check the file is genuine first, and only restore or exclude it if you're sure it's safe
questions.e: False positives do happen, but so do disguised malware files. Verify before trusting it.
